review.title: Don't Get Fooled Again: Pulitzer Winner Warns of Wall Street's Dark Side
review.summary: Eisman and journalist Gretchen Morgenson examine analyst conflicts, AIG accounting, mortgage securitization, dealer marks, due-diligence failures and private-equity incentives. Their strongest supported mechanisms concern compensation conflicts and the weakness of incomplete mortgage screening. Eisman rejects the claim that post-crisis banking never changed and explicitly refuses to forecast a private-equity or insurer collapse without data. Morgenson’s nursing-home and insurance warnings remain guest views. The audit qualifies retrospective accusations, sampling extrapolations and claims of absent regulation rather than treating indignation as proof.
review.assessment: Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Gretchen Morgenson. Direct agreement is recorded where explicit; her private-equity warnings are kept separate from his repeated refusal to predict a collapse.
framework_points: Trace incentives along the full origination and distribution chain.
Ask for executable prices when dealer model marks change.
Separate a legitimate hedge from misleading client disclosure.
Require recurring credit data before committing to a systemic short thesis.
Distinguish documented misconduct from proof of personal motive or criminal liability.
tools_and_charts: Clayton due-diligence samples and guideline exception rates
Floating-rate debt service and private-equity exit channels
transcript_cautions: Opening montage repeats later discussion.
The cash-in/cash-out swap anecdote contains explicitly uncertain contract recollections and invented numerical examples.
Clayton is sometimes captioned as Clayton Mortgage; the due-diligence firm is Clayton Holdings.
The guest corrects the suggestion that her reporting alone removed Greenberg.
Eisman corrects the guest’s nothing-changed claim and acknowledges available insurance statutory reports.
Neither participant gives a timed private-equity-collapse forecast attributed to Eisman.

claims.claim: Dot-com speculation combined with relentlessly positive sell-side research drew ordinary investors into companies without sustainable business economics.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Establish whether the stated dotcom research incentives proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: SEC investigations establish serious misleading-research conflicts. This does not establish that speculative enthusiasm always ends identically or quantify research’s share of total bubble losses.

evidence.title: Global Research Analyst Settlement testimony
evidence.finding: The SEC documents widespread analyst compensation linked to investment banking and misleading research, followed by settlements and separation requirements; not every analyst had an identical fee formula.

claims.next_check: Distinguish documented cases from a universal bubble rule.

claims.claim: Paying an analyst from underwriting revenue creates an incentive to promote an issuer even when the analyst doubts its quality.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish whether the stated analyst underwriting conflict proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.qualifications: His assertion of a universal identical percentage formula is broader than the inspected evidence.
claims.reason: The SEC documented investment-banking-linked compensation and enacted separation requirements addressing precisely this conflict. The economic conflict does not require every analyst to act dishonestly.

evidence.title: Global Research Analyst Settlement testimony
evidence.finding: The SEC documents widespread analyst compensation linked to investment banking and misleading research, followed by settlements and separation requirements; not every analyst had an identical fee formula.

claims.next_check: Review current compensation and disclosure rules for any contemporary application.

claims.claim: Some analysts recommended shares to customers while selling their own holdings, adding a personal trading conflict to the investment-banking conflict.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Match individual recommendations and personal transactions with enforcement findings; general research conflicts alone do not verify every personal-sale allegation.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: AIG’s decentralized operating companies, all ultimately dependent on Greenberg, became difficult to oversee as the group grew.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect consolidated risk systems and governance evidence for the relevant period; complexity alone does not identify the loss-generating activities.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: AIG marketed apparent insurance that merely spread a known loss over future periods without transferring genuine risk, enabling misleading financial statements.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish whether the stated aig sham risk transfer proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: The SEC’s Brightpoint action documents the same loss-smoothing mechanism and lack of substantive risk transfer. The transcript’s dollar amounts and ten-year schedule are explicitly illustrative.

evidence.title: Brightpoint and AIG accounting-fraud settlement
evidence.finding: AIG sold a purported insurance arrangement that smoothed known losses without genuine risk transfer. The SEC recorded a $10 million AIG penalty and $100,000 disgorgement; the example was a three-year arrangement.

claims.next_check: Retain the verified accounting mechanism rather than extrapolate to every AIG product.

claims.claim: The small penalty imposed on AIG for the loss-smoothing practice showed that regulators were ineffective deterrents.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare penalties, gains from misconduct and subsequent behavior; a normative claim of worthlessness has no objective threshold.
claims.reason: The Brightpoint penalty was $10 million rather than the roughly $25 million recollection. That numerical correction does not determine the optimal penalty or prove all regulation ineffective.

evidence.title: Brightpoint and AIG accounting-fraud settlement
evidence.finding: AIG sold a purported insurance arrangement that smoothed known losses without genuine risk transfer. The SEC recorded a $10 million AIG penalty and $100,000 disgorgement; the example was a three-year arrangement.

claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: The AIG rescue also protected Goldman and other derivative counterparties from losses that an AIG default could have imposed.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Establish whether the stated aig counterparty rescue proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: The FCIC documents interconnected counterparty exposures and the rescue. The episode’s reduction of the rescue to Goldman alone, and its precise hypothetical net loss, require collateral and hedge reconciliation.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, pages 350-352
evidence.finding: OTS had consolidated supervisory responsibility but failed to understand and supervise AIG Financial Products. OTC derivative products lacked normal capital and margin regulation; deficient oversight is distinct from no regulator.

claims.next_check: Reconcile gross payments, collateral already held, hedge collectability and the policyholder side of the rescue.

claims.claim: Greenberg’s pressure to maintain earnings growth after AIG became very large led to accounting manipulation.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Requires evidence linking the specific decisions to the alleged growth motive, not merely proof of accounting misconduct.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: Derivatives and synthetic CDOs multiplied exposure to an underlying stock of mortgages, amplifying the financial damage when those mortgages deteriorated.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish whether the stated synthetic exposure amplification proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.qualifications: The rough $500 billion annual origination figure is not treated as a precise estimate; gross notional is not net system loss.
claims.reason: For a fixed reference mortgage pool, multiple independent credit-default contracts can create multiple gross long and short exposures without additional mortgage origination. Losses are offset across counterparties before costs, but concentrated liabilities, leverage and default can amplify financial instability.
claims.next_check: Measure gross and net exposure and counterparty collateral separately.
claims.proof_assumptions: For a fixed reference mortgage pool, multiple independent credit-default contracts can create multiple gross long and short exposures without additional mortgage origination. Losses are offset across counterparties before costs, but concentrated liabilities, leverage and default can amplify financial instability.

proof.derivation: For a fixed reference mortgage pool, multiple independent credit-default contracts can create multiple gross long and short exposures without additional mortgage origination. Losses are offset across counterparties before costs, but concentrated liabilities, leverage and default can amplify financial instability.

claims.claim: Derivative demand also encouraged more mortgage origination, allowing the lending boom to grow beyond what ordinary loan demand would have supported.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Inspect contemporaneous securitizer purchase demand and originator funding; distinguish new mortgage finance from synthetic wagers on existing loans.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: Countrywide’s compensation gave loan officers incentives to steer borrowers into higher-paying subprime mortgages, including some who could qualify for prime loans.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Verify compensation schedules, borrower eligibility and steering outcomes; the two-to-three-times pay comparison requires dated records.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: Volume-linked fees throughout origination, ratings, packaging and distribution rewarded mortgage throughput while weakening incentives to reject poor underwriting.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Establish whether the stated mortgage assembly line proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: The FCIC’s investigative evidence documents the origination chain, fee incentives and deteriorating underwriting. This is a supported contributing mechanism rather than an exclusive explanation of the crisis.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13
evidence.finding: Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

claims.next_check: Retain the mechanism while separating each participant’s retained credit risk.

claims.claim: The housing crash caused far greater real-economy damage than the dot-com collapse because mortgage credit was tied to household balance sheets, housing activity and related spending.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Compare output, employment, household leverage and financial-sector transmission across the two episodes; the assertion that the dot-com collapse did not affect GDP is too categorical.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: AIG Financial Products was completely unregulated because AIG was an insurer.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Establish whether the stated aig unregulated absolute proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: OTC derivative products lacked normal capital and margin regulation, but OTS had consolidated authority and did examine the subsidiary inadequately. The absolute conflates ineffective supervision with absence of a regulator.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, pages 350-352
evidence.finding: OTS had consolidated supervisory responsibility but failed to understand and supervise AIG Financial Products. OTC derivative products lacked normal capital and margin regulation; deficient oversight is distinct from no regulator.

claims.next_check: Use the distinction between product deregulation and failed institutional supervision.

claims.claim: AIG’s mortgage credit-default commitments and related collateral demands were central to the liquidity crisis that forced its rescue.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish whether the stated aig cds failure proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.qualifications: The episode does not fully cover securities-lending losses, another relevant channel.
claims.reason: The FCIC identifies enormous unhedged CDS commitments without adequate initial collateral or reserves as a primary failure mechanism.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, pages 350-352
evidence.finding: OTS had consolidated supervisory responsibility but failed to understand and supervise AIG Financial Products. OTC derivative products lacked normal capital and margin regulation; deficient oversight is distinct from no regulator.

claims.next_check: Include other funding demands when reconstructing total liquidity needs.

claims.claim: Dealer-controlled marks on bilateral derivatives can create a severe information and bargaining disadvantage for the counterparty facing collateral demands.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish whether the stated dealer marking conflict proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: The FCIC identifies opaque OTC price discovery as exacerbating Goldman-AIG collateral disputes. Eisman explicitly concedes that Goldman may have been economically right about the mortgage prices.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, pages 350-352
evidence.finding: OTS had consolidated supervisory responsibility but failed to understand and supervise AIG Financial Products. OTC derivative products lacked normal capital and margin regulation; deficient oversight is distinct from no regulator.

claims.next_check: Compare executable two-way prices, contractual valuation terms and independent marks.

claims.claim: An unexplained Goldman repricing and extremely wide two-way quote undermined Eisman’s confidence in the reliability of dealer marks during 2007.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Obtain trade confirmations and executable quotes from the episode; the speaker acknowledges he cannot now reconstruct the contract details.
claims.qualifications: Illustrative prices of 70, 80 and 50 are not audited trade records; no specific hidden motive is asserted.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: Goldman was entitled to hedge its own mortgage risk, but continuing to sell products it viewed negatively to clients created an unacceptable client conflict.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish whether the stated goldman client counterparty conflict proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: The ABACUS settlement independently establishes a serious disclosure failure involving an adverse short investor. It does not prove that taking the opposite side of a fully disclosed transaction is itself fraudulent or that every mortgage sale shared the defect.

evidence.title: Goldman Sachs ABACUS settlement
evidence.finding: Goldman paid $550 million and acknowledged incomplete disclosure of Paulson’s adverse economic interest and portfolio-selection role. The firm settled without admitting or denying the charges; Tourre litigation continued.

claims.next_check: Evaluate disclosure, suitability and selection conflicts transaction by transaction.

claims.claim: Regulators concentrated on lower-level individuals such as Tourre while failing to hold the executives directing the businesses personally accountable.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Compare civil and criminal enforcement across responsible individuals and firms; absence of a criminal conviction alone does not establish the regulator’s motive.
claims.qualifications: The SEC also brought a firm-level Goldman action; the criticism concerns senior individual accountability, not literally no action.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: Clayton found widespread violations of underwriting guidelines in mortgage samples that securitizers had purchased.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish whether the stated clayton defects proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.qualifications: A guideline defect is not identical to inevitable default or loss.
claims.reason: The FCIC records 28% of 911,039 reviewed loans as deficient without approved compensating factors over the 18 months to June 2007.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, pages 165-167 and 335-336
evidence.finding: Clayton data show 28% of reviewed loans deficient and 39% of those waived in; samples varied and were not always random. Barclays rescue faced FSA approval and shareholder-guarantee obstacles, complicating a single-cause Paulson explanation.

claims.next_check: Retain the specific reviewed sample and grading definition.

claims.claim: A defect rate of roughly 20% to 50% in sampled mortgages implied a similar defect rate in the unreviewed remainder.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish whether the stated clayton sample extrapolation proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: The FCIC found pervasive defects but explains that some samples targeted likely problem loans rather than being random. A comparable population rate is a reasonable concern, not a mathematically assured inference for every pool.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, pages 165-167 and 335-336
evidence.finding: Clayton data show 28% of reviewed loans deficient and 39% of those waived in; samples varied and were not always random. Barclays rescue faced FSA approval and shareholder-guarantee obstacles, complicating a single-cause Paulson explanation.

claims.next_check: Obtain pool-level sampling designs and confidence intervals before making a precise extrapolation.

claims.claim: Ratings agencies were offered Clayton’s exception information but declined it because incorporating the information threatened ratings and fee income.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Establish whether the stated ratings data incentive proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.qualifications: The causal motive is supported by witness testimony, not a finding that every rating analyst had the same intent.
claims.reason: The FCIC records Clayton president Keith Johnson’s testimony that agencies rejected the offered data and his explanation of the commercial conflict.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, pages 165-167 and 335-336
evidence.finding: Clayton data show 28% of reviewed loans deficient and 39% of those waived in; samples varied and were not always random. Barclays rescue faced FSA approval and shareholder-guarantee obstacles, complicating a single-cause Paulson explanation.

claims.next_check: Keep the attribution to the documented witness account.

claims.claim: Removing only detected defective loans left unexamined mortgages in securitized pools, so limited due diligence did not assure the remaining pool met its representations.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish whether the stated partial sampling securitization proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.qualifications: The $1 billion pool, 10% sample and 25% defect rate are illustrative; some known defective loans were also waived back in.
claims.reason: The FCIC documents limited samples, waived-in deficient loans and inadequate disclosure. Independently, removing detected defects from a subset cannot establish that the untested remainder has no defects.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, pages 165-167 and 335-336
evidence.finding: Clayton data show 28% of reviewed loans deficient and 39% of those waived in; samples varied and were not always random. Barclays rescue faced FSA approval and shareholder-guarantee obstacles, complicating a single-cause Paulson explanation.

claims.next_check: Check pool-specific warranties, waivers and actual investor disclosures.

claims.claim: The Clayton disclosures represented exceptionally serious fraud, and the failure to prosecute senior people after referral showed a failure of accountability.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect the actual criminal referral, prosecutorial decisions, legal elements and subsequent cases; seriousness of defective disclosure does not by itself establish a prosecutable individual case.
claims.qualifications: The superlative biggest fraud is rhetorical; the guest and host admit they do not know the exact decision chain.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: The lack of senior criminal accountability after the crisis deepened the public belief that financial elites face a different justice system, with lasting political consequences.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Requires evidence linking perceived accountability to political attitudes and outcomes, not merely the temporal sequence of crisis and polarization.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: It is incorrect to say nothing changed after 2008: tighter capital and leverage oversight materially reduced the banking system’s risk.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish whether the stated postcrisis deleveraging proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.qualifications: His stated Tarullo tenure and title are approximate; lower bank risk does not eliminate nonbank risk.
claims.reason: The stress-test evidence demonstrates substantial capital and modeled resilience. It does not independently verify the precise Citigroup 40-to-10 comparison or assign all change to Tarullo.

evidence.title: 2025 stress-test results, revised September 30
evidence.finding: Aggregate CET1 13.4% at start, hypothetical trough 11.6%; institution-specific outcomes and separate leverage ratios are disclosed. Results reflect scenario, portfolio and model assumptions, not a direct measure of political intent.

claims.next_check: Compare consistent assets-to-common-equity and off-balance-sheet metrics before and after the reforms.

claims.claim: Private-equity ownership of nursing homes has been associated with an approximately 10% increase in short-term patient mortality.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Establish whether the stated pe nursing mortality proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: The inspected primary author abstract and journal result report an approximately 11% local treatment effect among Medicare patients. This supports the approximate cited result, not a universal effect at every facility; the full methodology could not be fetched.

evidence.title: Owner Incentives and Performance in Healthcare
evidence.publisher: Atul Gupta, Sabrina Howell, Constantine Yannelis and Abhinav Gupta / NBER
evidence.finding: Inspected indexed author abstract and primary journal result: estimated local treatment effect on short-term Medicare mortality is about 11%, using an instrument for patient-facility matching. Full paper fetch was blocked, so detailed identification assumptions were not independently audited.

claims.next_check: Inspect the complete study identification assumptions, sample and heterogeneity before stronger causal generalization.

claims.claim: Private-equity pressure to raise exit value can reduce nursing staff and care quality, making financial incentives directly relevant to patient outcomes.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Match acquisition effects on staffing and patient risk with study designs that address selection and confounding; profit incentives alone do not prove harm at every facility.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: Apollo’s aluminum-smelter investment extracted large dividends through added debt, after which the company struggled and failed.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Reconcile original equity, debt-funded distributions, commodity-price changes, costs and bankruptcy records; leverage contribution must be separated from other shocks.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: The smelter failure harmed employees, the local tax base, schools and pensioners even though the private-equity sponsor had already recovered substantial cash.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Establish whether the stated noranda external costs proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: PBGC records confirm a Noranda pension plan entered trusteeship in 2016. The inspected primary record does not establish the entire jobs, electricity-rate, school-insurance and sponsor-return account.

evidence.finding: PBGC records termination October 31, 2016 and trusteeship November 9, with 1,364 participants. This establishes one pension takeover, not every alleged community consequence or the cause of bankruptcy.

claims.next_check: Inspect the bankruptcy, utility-rate orders, municipal budgets and all three pension plans.

claims.claim: Private-equity hospital acquisitions can worsen care when financial restructuring and cost cuts fall on already fragile rural institutions.

claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.

claims.claim: Private-equity distress is increasing because higher floating interest costs and weak exit markets undermine a model that benefited from cheap debt and easy sales.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Track defaults and restructurings against a defined PE-backed borrower universe, interest coverage, hedges and exit proceeds; anecdotes alone cannot establish system-wide collapse.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.

claims.claim: For an unhedged borrower with floating-rate debt, a higher reference rate raises debt service and reduces cash available for equity holders.
claims.speaker: Gretchen Morgenson
claims.test: Establish whether the stated floating debt service proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: Assume unchanged debt principal, spread and interest floor, no hedge and a reference-rate reset. Interest equals principal times reference rate plus spread, so a higher reference rate raises expense. The transcript’s assertion that all PE debt is floating is not required for the relationship.
claims.next_check: Measure fixed-rate shares, floors, caps and hedges for actual borrowers.

Interest equals principal times reference rate plus spread, so a higher reference rate raises expense. The transcript’s assertion that all PE debt is floating is not required for the relationship.

review.title: Big Beautiful Bill, Write-Off Revolution & Tariff Tempest - The Friday Market Wrap!
review.summary: A short host market wrap is followed by a substantial July 9 interview with Dan Clifton about the newly enacted tax and spending law. The guest argues that business deductions and household tax relief can offset tariff damage, identifies sector beneficiaries, and expects a one-percentage-point growth contribution. The report separates those guest forecasts from Eisman questions and endorsements.
review.assessment: The interview identifies real tax incentives, but often overstates scope or certainty. Full expensing does not make an asset free, all data-center buildings do not qualify as factories, the rural fund is $50 billion, and several Medicaid changes start before 2028. The orphan-drug misunderstanding is corrected within the conversation and is not scored as an asserted Eisman claim.
framework_points: Trace a policy change into after-tax cash flow and customer spending.
Analyze tariff costs and tax relief together, with consistent baselines.
Separate a policy preference from the investment effect of enacted law.
Check legal eligibility before extrapolating a sector boom.
transcript_cautions: Dan Clifton interview recorded July 9; the host wrap is dated July 11.
Host questions about company-wide orphan-drug exemptions are corrected by the guest and excluded from asserted-claim scoring.
Most tax-policy projections belong to Clifton, not Eisman.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman hosts through 553 seconds. Dan Clifton provides the policy presentation from approximately 645 seconds, with host questions and occasional explicit endorsements.

claims.claim: Upcoming large-bank results should be generally uneventful, with strong trading revenue.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare large-bank revenue components and guidance changes.
claims.reason: JPMorgan reported strong markets revenue, supporting the specific trading component. Uneventful is subjective and misses meaningful differences in individual bank guidance.

evidence.title: JPMorgan second-quarter 2025 results
evidence.finding: Markets revenue reached $8.9 billion amid elevated volatility. Results support the near-term trading-revenue forecast, not every part of an uneventful bank season.

claims.next_check: Compare large-bank revenue components and guidance changes.

claims.claim: Out-of-the-money index puts can hedge a bullish portfolio while limiting option loss to the premium.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Specify contracts, premium, exposure and protection interval.
claims.reason: For purchased puts, terminal payoff is nonnegative and the maximum standalone option loss is the premium. Protection depends on strike, expiry, sizing and portfolio basis risk.
claims.next_check: Specify contracts, premium, exposure and protection interval.

assumptions: Purchased puts, not written options
No unrelated financing liabilities
proof.derivation: At expiry, put payoff is max(strike-index,0). Net option P&L is payoff minus premium, so its maximum loss is the premium; portfolio loss can remain larger than the hedge payoff.

claims.claim: Index puts are the only way to hedge a US downturn.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare portfolio delta, drawdowns and carrying costs under specified hedges.
claims.reason: The payoff claim does not make puts unique: reducing equity exposure or holding offsetting exposure can also reduce market sensitivity. Their costs and risks differ.
claims.next_check: Compare portfolio delta, drawdowns and carrying costs under specified hedges.

assumptions: Hedge means reducing sensitivity to a market decline
proof.derivation: Reducing a positive equity position reduces its downside exposure without purchasing a put. Therefore the set of possible risk reductions is not limited to index puts.

claims.claim: The rally does not require a secret government or market-maker manipulation theory.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Require affirmative evidence of coordinated trades or instructions before attributing market moves.
claims.reason: This is rejection of an unsupported explanation, not proof that no manipulation ever occurs.
claims.next_check: Require affirmative evidence of coordinated trades or instructions before attributing market moves.

claims.claim: Money market funds are distinct from FDIC-insured deposits and may contain different types of short-term assets.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Read the fund mandate, holdings, fees and legal protections.
claims.reason: The SEC describes these distinctions and potential losses. A money market deposit account is a different product from a mutual fund.

evidence.title: Money market fund risks
evidence.finding: Money market funds lack FDIC insurance and can lose value. Government-backed portfolio securities do not turn fund shares into insured bank deposits.

claims.next_check: Read the fund mandate, holdings, fees and legal protections.

claims.claim: A Treasury-only money market fund effectively provides the same protection as FDIC insurance.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Distinguish portfolio credit risk from guarantees on the investor claim.
claims.reason: Treasury assets have government credit backing, but fund shares are not insured deposits and retain fund, pricing and operational risks.

evidence.title: Money market fund risks
evidence.finding: Money market funds lack FDIC insurance and can lose value. Government-backed portfolio securities do not turn fund shares into insured bank deposits.

claims.next_check: Distinguish portfolio credit risk from guarantees on the investor claim.

claims.claim: Permanent extension of key individual tax provisions removes the scheduled year-end tax cliff.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Compare prior sunset dates and enacted extensions.
claims.reason: The enacted law extended key provisions, eliminating their planned expiration. This does not make every provision of the package permanent.

evidence.title: 2025 reconciliation tax provisions
evidence.finding: The law restored domestic research expensing and modified business deductions. Eligibility, timing and limitations remain relevant; a deduction is not a dollar-for-dollar reimbursement.

claims.next_check: Compare prior sunset dates and enacted extensions.

claims.claim: The law delivers relief on tips, overtime, seniors and auto-loan payments.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Read each eligibility rule, cap and sunset.
claims.reason: There are real deductions, but auto relief applies to qualifying interest, not all principal payments; income, amount and time limits apply across these provisions.

evidence.title: Deductions for workers and seniors
evidence.finding: Tips, qualifying overtime, seniors and qualifying vehicle-loan interest receive capped, income-limited deductions. These are not universal exemptions for all income or all loan payments.

claims.next_check: Read each eligibility rule, cap and sunset.

claims.claim: Household refunds and tax relief will deliver more than $100 billion of consumer support in early 2026.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Compare 2026 refunds and disposable income with a no-law baseline.
claims.reason: The timing mechanism is plausible, but the exact incremental amount and spending response require tax-return data and a consistent counterfactual.
claims.next_check: Compare 2026 refunds and disposable income with a no-law baseline.

claims.claim: Business tax deductions can offset enough tariff damage to prevent recession.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Estimate tariffs, tax changes, distribution and timing jointly.
claims.reason: The beneficiaries and timing of deductions differ from those bearing tariff costs. No common macro model or magnitude establishes complete offset.
claims.next_check: Estimate tariffs, tax changes, distribution and timing jointly.

claims.claim: Tax cuts can offset price increases from tariffs.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Measure after-tax income, pass-through and demand separately.
claims.reason: Eisman explicitly restates the guest mechanism, but a dollar of firm tax relief does not mechanically cancel a dollar of consumer price increases.
claims.next_check: Measure after-tax income, pass-through and demand separately.

claims.claim: All factories and data centers can immediately expense their entire building cost.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Distinguish equipment deductions from the special building provision and test eligible uses.
claims.reason: Qualifying production-property expensing is real, but the tangible-product and use restrictions exclude a blanket rule for all data-center real estate or every part of a factory.

evidence.title: Qualified production property guidance
evidence.finding: Section 168(n) concerns qualifying production of tangible products and excludes office, research and software-development portions. General data-center real estate is not automatically a qualifying factory.

claims.next_check: Distinguish equipment deductions from the special building provision and test eligible uses.

claims.claim: Immediate expensing makes a factory roughly 30% cheaper and completely eliminates tariff effects.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Model incremental present-value tax savings against actual tariff exposure.
claims.reason: Accelerating deductions can improve present value, but the saving depends on tax rate, tax capacity and the previous deduction schedule. It cannot generically eliminate an unrelated tariff bill.

evidence.title: Qualified production property guidance
evidence.finding: Section 168(n) concerns qualifying production of tangible products and excludes office, research and software-development portions. General data-center real estate is not automatically a qualifying factory.

claims.next_check: Model incremental present-value tax savings against actual tariff exposure.

claims.claim: Permanent full expensing of qualifying equipment should stimulate industrial equipment orders.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Compare qualifying equipment orders and user cost with a no-law baseline.
claims.reason: Eligibility and incentive direction are clear, but incremental orders versus purchases merely shifted forward require observed investment data.
claims.next_check: Compare qualifying equipment orders and user cost with a no-law baseline.

claims.claim: Domestic research expensing benefits technology, pharmaceutical and industrial firms.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Compare qualified domestic spending and cash taxes.
claims.reason: IRS guidance confirms immediate domestic research deductions, while foreign research remains on a different schedule. The tax benefit does not prove a stock-price gain.

evidence.title: 2025 reconciliation tax provisions
evidence.finding: The law restored domestic research expensing and modified business deductions. Eligibility, timing and limitations remain relevant; a deduction is not a dollar-for-dollar reimbursement.

claims.next_check: Compare qualified domestic spending and cash taxes.

claims.claim: Changing the business-interest limit from an EBIT to EBITDA basis permits larger deductions.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Reconcile adjusted taxable income and deductible interest.
claims.reason: Holding other inputs constant, adding depreciation and amortization increases the earnings base used for a percentage limit. Actual deductibility still depends on statutory adjustments and exceptions.
claims.next_check: Reconcile adjusted taxable income and deductible interest.

assumptions: Nonnegative depreciation and amortization
Same percentage limit and other adjustments
proof.derivation: EBITDA equals EBIT plus depreciation and amortization. Thirty percent of the larger base is at least thirty percent of EBIT, increasing capacity when the limit binds.

claims.claim: Spending reductions in energy, Medicaid, nutrition and student loans create losers alongside tax beneficiaries.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Map provisions to outlays, coverage, loan availability and sector revenues.
claims.reason: The broad policy tradeoff is real, but the stated category totals and privatization effects need a consistent score and actual eligibility changes.
claims.next_check: Map provisions to outlays, coverage, loan availability and sector revenues.

claims.claim: A gradual Treasury General Account refill should reduce disruption from debt issuance.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Track bills, coupons, reserve balances and money-market funding conditions.
claims.reason: Issuance composition and buyers matter along with pace. The transcript does not supply a counterfactual market-impact estimate.
claims.next_check: Track bills, coupons, reserve balances and money-market funding conditions.

claims.claim: The bill and tariffs together keep deficits around 6.2%-6.3% of GDP rather than making the deficit worse.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Build a common baseline, annual path and sensitivity to growth, interest and legal changes.
claims.reason: The quoted CBO scores use different windows and assumptions. Stable annual deficit/GDP does not follow from subtracting cumulative estimates, and future tariff policy is uncertain.

evidence.title: Deficit effects of Public Law 119-21
evidence.finding: The enacted legislation adds about $3.4 trillion to 2025-2034 deficits before macroeconomic and debt-service effects. That is a baseline-relative score, not a stable annual deficit/GDP forecast.

evidence.title: Budget and economic effects of tariffs through May 13, 2025
evidence.finding: CBO estimated $2.8 trillion of deficit reduction over 2025-2035 after economic effects, conditional on the tariff schedule. This differs in window and assumptions from the bill score.

claims.next_check: Build a common baseline, annual path and sensitivity to growth, interest and legal changes.

claims.claim: High interest costs have forced the first US fiscal austerity in 30 years.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Define cyclically adjusted fiscal tightening and compare prior episodes.
claims.reason: Austerity is defined by the guest as tariffs financing extensions of existing tax cuts. The historical superlative and threshold are not based on a specified fiscal-impulse measure.
claims.next_check: Define cyclically adjusted fiscal tightening and compare prior episodes.

claims.claim: Factory expensing, domestic R&D deductions and broader orphan-drug exclusions make pharma more attractive.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Estimate company-specific cash-tax and negotiated-price exposure.
claims.reason: Real deductions and a broader product-specific exclusion support the policy benefit. Overall attractiveness also depends on prices, clinical pipelines, tariffs and valuation.

evidence.title: 2025 reconciliation tax provisions
evidence.finding: The law restored domestic research expensing and modified business deductions. Eligibility, timing and limitations remain relevant; a deduction is not a dollar-for-dollar reimbursement.

evidence.title: Qualified production property guidance
evidence.finding: Section 168(n) concerns qualifying production of tangible products and excludes office, research and software-development portions. General data-center real estate is not automatically a qualifying factory.

evidence.title: 2028 drug negotiation guidance
evidence.finding: The law expands the exclusion for a drug designated for one or more rare diseases if all approved indications meet the rare-disease condition. It is not an exemption for all drugs owned by a company.

claims.next_check: Estimate company-specific cash-tax and negotiated-price exposure.

claims.claim: The orphan-drug exclusion expands to drugs with multiple rare-disease indications, rather than exempting whole companies.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Check each drug and all approved indications.
claims.reason: The guest clarifies the host misunderstanding within the exchange. CMS guidance confirms that the exclusion applies to qualifying products and indications.

evidence.title: 2028 drug negotiation guidance
evidence.finding: The law expands the exclusion for a drug designated for one or more rare diseases if all approved indications meet the rare-disease condition. It is not an exemption for all drugs owned by a company.

claims.next_check: Check each drug and all approved indications.

claims.claim: Medicaid is essentially emergency care, and eligibility tightening mostly removes waste rather than valuable coverage.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Compare covered services and outcomes for affected populations.
claims.reason: This is a broad evaluative characterization, not established by budget arithmetic. Enrollment loss, access, health outcomes and administrative churn need direct evidence.
claims.next_check: Compare covered services and outcomes for affected populations.

claims.claim: Medicaid cuts and eligibility changes do not start until 2028.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Check each provision effective date rather than one date for the package.
claims.reason: Some provider-financing changes phase in later, but work requirements begin by January 2027 and other provisions have their own dates. The blanket timing assurance is false.

evidence.title: Medicaid reform implementation guidance
evidence.finding: Work requirements must be implemented by January 1, 2027, with earlier state implementation possible. Not all Medicaid changes wait until 2028.

claims.next_check: Check each provision effective date rather than one date for the package.

claims.claim: A roughly $100 billion rural hospital stabilization fund mitigates the cuts.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Compare statutory appropriation, allocation and affected providers.
claims.reason: The enacted Rural Health Transformation Program totals $50 billion over five fiscal years. Its existence also does not quantify how much of the broader funding loss it offsets.

evidence.title: Rural Health Transformation Program
evidence.finding: The statute allocates $50 billion over fiscal years 2026-2030, not $100 billion.

claims.next_check: Compare statutory appropriation, allocation and affected providers.

claims.claim: Full expensing means companies can buy or build eligible assets for free.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Calculate tax saving at the applicable marginal rate.
claims.reason: A deduction reduces taxable income, not cost dollar for dollar. The guest earlier mentions a partial tax saving, but the later free wording is materially misleading.
claims.next_check: Calculate tax saving at the applicable marginal rate.

assumptions: Positive cost C
Tax rate t below 100%
Sufficient taxable income to use the deduction
proof.derivation: An immediate deduction saves t times C in current tax, leaving a cash cost C times (1-t). Relative to future depreciation, the incremental benefit is smaller than the entire immediate deduction value.

claims.claim: Industrials, materials and selected software providers will gain from a capex boom; factory construction could surge even if some facilities later sit empty.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Track orders, construction spending, utilization and a predeclared beneficiary basket.
claims.reason: The sector forecast has no fixed basket or return horizon, and announcements are not completed capital expenditure. Ghost-factory wording is an acknowledged downside scenario.
claims.next_check: Track orders, construction spending, utilization and a predeclared beneficiary basket.

claims.claim: The law adds about one percentage point to GDP growth, front-loaded into 2025-2026, largely sterilizing tariffs.
claims.speaker: Dan Clifton
claims.test: Estimate the law-only contribution over the stated period using a consistent macro model.
claims.reason: Full-year 2026 is incomplete at the cutoff, and the incremental effect requires a counterfactual rather than simply observing GDP growth.
claims.next_check: Estimate the law-only contribution over the stated period using a consistent macro model.

review.title: Why the Market's Surging Despite the Headlines
review.summary: Chris Verrone argues that broad participation, subdued sentiment and cyclical leadership support further gains after the April rebound. His six- and twelve-month S&P direction proved right, while his H2 gold reversal failed. Eisman retains tariff concerns, advances a regional-bank consolidation thesis and explains AI demand for power and cooling. He raises software-moat risks and distinguishes Bitcoin profits from proof of a hedge thesis. The episode rewards separating signal, mechanism and outcome: successful index forecasts do not validate every chart narrative or transfer guest calls to Eisman.
review.assessment: Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Chris Verrone. Explicit agreement and separate host theses are captured individually. Short acknowledgments and requests for explanation are not treated as adoption of every guest target.
framework_points: Compare market breadth and sentiment with capitalization-weighted indexes.
Use historical conditional patterns while acknowledging small samples and exceptions.
Separate economic forecasts from asset-return forecasts.
Map AI demand into physical infrastructure and incumbent software competition.
A correct security return does not prove the proposed causal story.
tools_and_charts: Put/call ratios, investor surveys and fund flows
transcript_cautions: Recorded July 7, 2025, published July 14; both dates matter for returns.
Eisman says February 29 although 2025 has no such date; the guest supplies February 19.
Chart images are not in the text; proprietary breadth and backtests were not independently reconstructed.
The historical drawdown threshold is explicitly relaxed from 15% to 5% to expand the sample.
Verrone immediately mentions Mitsubishi after Eisman’s two-supplier gas-turbine claim.
Guest gold, dollar and foreign-equity calls are not automatically Eisman endorsements.

review.summary: Eisman uses the first earnings week to demonstrate thesis checking and bank valuation. He compares tangible-equity returns across major banks, distinguishes earnings beats from stock reactions, and explains his move from GFC bearishness to a predominantly long US portfolio. Corporate observations are contemporaneous diagnoses, not newly successful forecasts.
review.assessment: His best contribution is relating bank profitability to valuation while explicitly acknowledging exceptions. The stronger claims about permanent safety, unique US technology exposure and Citi never recovering an old price are not precise, finite predictions. Earnings-season evidence supports resilience but does not make tariffs the only possible risk.
framework_points: Use earnings to test a thesis rather than guess the next trading-day reaction.
Compare sustainable ROTCE with price to tangible book, then explain exceptions.
Separate recurring income from reserve releases and investment gains.
Update a market stance when bank leverage and the opportunity set change.

review.title: The Secrets of the Short Seller: How the Pros Spot Trouble
review.summary: Lakshmi Ganapathy explains shorts in Stellantis, solar suppliers and Opendoor, then reviews mistakes in Reddit and DraftKings and the dangers of cult stocks. Eisman presses for company-specific causes rather than generic industry weakness and endorses avoiding valuation-only shorts. His financing and negative-equity explanations are coherent. Product-failure allegations and historical trade returns remain unverified. The First Solar discussion contains a material error: manufacturing credits did not disappear on the claimed 2028 schedule. Correct stock direction would not validate that policy premise or the guest’s dramatic failure-rate estimates.
review.assessment: Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Lakshmi Ganapathy of Unicus Research. The guest’s price targets, unverified allegations and reported historical returns are distinct from the host’s questions and explicit methodological endorsements.
framework_points: Require a specific company mechanism rather than merely a weak sector.
Use channel checks, while checking their sample and denominators.
Distinguish short timing and solvency from eventual business value.
Avoid valuation alone and recognize emotionally driven investor bases.
Separate product quality, financing, demand and policy explanations.
transcript_cautions: The airline is deliberately unnamed and no identity is inferred.
The EV battery percentage wording is ambiguous and is not treated as a reliable cost estimate.
The guest corrects the SolarEdge initiation price from $280 to $329.
SolarEdge and Enphase product-failure figures lack a consistent disclosed denominator or time horizon.
The SolarEdge earnings squeeze date and point moves are explicitly uncertain.
The guest stops following Reddit and withdraws DraftKings; those are revisions, not maintained current shorts.
Eisman’s repeated First Solar credit-expiration statement is assessed against Section 45X, not conflated with household solar credits.

review.title: Meme Stock Resurgence: Warning Signs or Just Noise? - The Friday Market Wrap!
review.summary: The July 25 earnings tour distinguishes T-Mobile growth from legacy telecom, Charter competitive pressure, homebuilder relief rallies and the spread of AI demand into power equipment and connectors. Eisman also warns about meme-stock speculation while retaining his long-term bullish stance.
review.assessment: Several operating diagnoses are well supported, especially cable competition, builder margin pressure and AI supply-chain demand. The Enphase comparison is materially wrong, the gas-turbine supplier count omits Mitsubishi, and Fiserv revenue and EPS guidance should not be conflated. His Chipotle and meme-stock cautions lack fixed forecast horizons.
framework_points: Compare competitors inside one industry before treating the sector as homogeneous.
Separate a relief rally from improving fundamentals.
Look for AI beneficiaries outside semiconductor leaders.
Track same-store sales and margins rather than only earnings beats.
Treat short squeezes as positioning events until business evidence changes.
tools_and_charts: Cable broadband losses and mobile gains
transcript_cautions: Enphase narrative compares Q2 2025 with a much earlier revenue peak, despite saying the same quarter last year.
Charter 111,000 refers to residential Internet customers; total losses were 117,000.
Guest short recommendations and unverified claimed short returns are not credited as Eisman trades.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

claims.reason: The issuer reported strong postpaid phone net additions. The operating evidence supports customer growth, not every assertion about network quality or lowest underlying cost.

evidence.title: T-Mobile Q2 2025 results
evidence.finding: Postpaid phone net additions reached 830,000, supporting continued customer gains. This does not independently establish best quality or lowest cost on every dimension.

claims.next_check: Track subscriber gains, churn, service margins and capital intensity.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track broadband churn, pricing, mobile gains and cash returns on network upgrades.
claims.reason: Customer losses and mobile expansion show overlapping competitive markets. Slight revenue and EBITDA growth qualify the literal claim of no growth at all.

evidence.title: Charter Q2 2025 results
evidence.finding: Residential Internet customers fell 111,000 and total Internet customers fell 117,000. Revenue and adjusted EBITDA still grew slightly, so customer contraction is not identical to zero growth in every financial measure.

claims.next_check: Track broadband churn, pricing, mobile gains and cash returns on network upgrades.

evidence.title: D.R. Horton fiscal Q3 2025 results
evidence.finding: EPS declined 18%, with full-year closings guidance of 85,000-85,500. The release supports weak underlying conditions despite a positive stock reaction.

claims.next_check: Compare orders, incentives and margins with prior periods and expectations.

evidence.finding: GM North America costs included $1.1 billion of tariff impact, increased warranty costs and unfavorable EV-related inventory adjustments.

evidence.finding: Adjusted diluted EPS rose to $0.81 from $0.44. Management described strong IT datacom demand and raised its outlook.

claims.reason: Unassailable is an indefinite competitive judgment. The episode supplies no valuation or market-share threshold that would resolve it.
claims.next_check: Track network take rates, payment volumes, regulation and alternative rails.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate revenue and EPS revisions and compare like-for-like market growth.
claims.reason: Organic revenue growth guidance narrowed toward the low end, but EPS guidance increased its lower bound. Slower growth alone does not establish share loss without a market denominator.

evidence.title: Fiserv Q2 2025 results
evidence.finding: The outlook narrowed organic revenue growth to about 10%, while adjusted EPS guidance narrowed to $10.15-$10.30 from $10.10-$10.30. Revenue and EPS guidance moved differently.

claims.next_check: Separate revenue and EPS revisions and compare like-for-like market growth.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track search revenue, query economics, cloud margins and AI monetization.
claims.reason: Search and cloud growth support the current operating diagnosis. The long-term disruption question remains unresolved and is acknowledged as such.

evidence.finding: Search revenue grew 12% and cloud revenue 32%. Contemporary operating growth did not settle the long-term competitive effect of AI.

claims.next_check: Track search revenue, query economics, cloud margins and AI monetization.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

claims.reason: Comparable sales fell 4%, supporting the operating concern. The conditional derating forecast has no target or deadline and is not automatically resolved by that same quarter weakness.

evidence.finding: Comparable restaurant sales declined 4.0%. New restaurants still supported aggregate revenue growth, so same-store sales and total sales must be separated.

claims.claim: Large price moves caused by short squeezes can be hazardous without corresponding business improvement.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

claims.next_check: Separate operating news from positioning and size positions for reversal risk.

assumptions: The price move is driven by forced covering rather than changed expected cash flows
proof.derivation: Temporary share demand can raise price without increasing intrinsic cash generation. When that temporary demand ends, the supporting flow can disappear even though the business is unchanged.

review.title: How a Short Seller Succeeds: The Blueprint for Strategy and Survival
review.summary: Eisman and Brad Safalow examine short-selling risk through Freshpet, Trupanion and Kinsale. Eisman discloses a Trupanion short, endorses its apparent deterioration and insists on catalysts and surviving countertrend rallies. Most detailed allegations and forecasts belong to Safalow. Later results support slower Freshpet growth and Kinsale premium pressure but contradict the predicted Kinsale underwriting deterioration and weaken Trupanion’s collapse narrative. The interview is strongest on trade-path risk and the difference between fundamental conviction and realized returns.
review.assessment: Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.
review.speaker_map_notes: Eisman hosts and asks catalyst questions; Brad Safalow gives detailed short theses. Eisman explicitly endorses the Trupanion deterioration premise and short-path risk, but does not adopt Kinsale fraud or insolvency allegations. Safalow specifically disclaims fraud and a zero target for Kinsale.
framework_points: Separate company deterioration from profitable trade execution.
Demand a catalyst rather than shorting solely on valuation.
Inspect insurance cohorts, state filings and policy exclusions.
Account for flows and positioning but do not assume they identify every price cause.

review.title: How Tariff Deals, Pharma Shocks, & Mega Mergers Redefined the Market - The Friday Market Wrap!
review.summary: The August 1 wrap, uploaded August 2, keeps trade policy at the center of the macro outlook while reviewing strong AI-related earnings and weak managed-care and cable results. It also explains Eisman portfolio practice: buy the intended position and hold while the business thesis survives, with less attention to valuation.
review.assessment: The company-level distinctions are often useful, especially Starbucks and broadband weakness versus AI growth. Broader conclusions are less secure: tariff news is not isolated as the sole cause of market declines, a rail deal is not pre-approved, and a high free-cash-flow yield does not mathematically imply bankruptcy.
framework_points: Separate current results from market expectations.
Distinguish a turnaround narrative from measured operating recovery.
Use thesis failure as a sell trigger.
Treat announced policy and transactions separately from implementation.
transcript_cautions: The source explicitly refers to Friday August 1 despite its August 2 upload.
The UNH 2024 guidance reference is a spoken date error; the discussion concerns 2025.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.claim: Germany may suffer most from the EU tariff settlement because of its export dependence.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare country-specific US value-added exports and realized sector effects.
claims.reason: This is explicitly a guess; aggregate export dependence does not measure US exposure, value added or substitution.
claims.next_check: Compare country-specific US value-added exports and realized sector effects.

claims.claim: The economy remains strong, and trade war is the key threat despite several agreements.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Define trade-war severity and macro outcomes before scoring.
claims.reason: The conditional macro view lacks a tariff threshold and economic-outcome horizon. It should not be interpreted as a guarantee against other shocks.
claims.next_check: Define trade-war severity and macro outcomes before scoring.

claims.claim: The full economic consequences of higher tariffs may take years to become apparent.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track multi-year prices, investment, sourcing and real income.
claims.reason: The long-run adjustment period is not complete at the cutoff. Price, sourcing and capital-allocation effects can occur on different schedules.
claims.next_check: Track multi-year prices, investment, sourcing and real income.

claims.claim: The entire weekly equity correction was caused by tariff news.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use event timing and a multi-factor analysis rather than assign the full move to one headline.
claims.reason: The same wrap discusses a major payroll disappointment and earnings surprises. No identification method separates those drivers.
claims.next_check: Use event timing and a multi-factor analysis rather than assign the full move to one headline.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate official approval, private assurances and aggregate deal activity.
claims.reason: The wink-and-nod claim lacks direct evidence; the STB was still reviewing the application in October 2026. A broader advisory cycle must be measured independently.

evidence.title: STB denies summary-denial motions in UP-NS proceeding
evidence.finding: The merger remained in regulatory consideration in October 2026. A filed deal and procedural acceptance are not final approval or proof of a private political assurance.

claims.next_check: Separate official approval, private assurances and aggregate deal activity.

claims.claim: Goldman, Evercore and PJT could benefit from a stronger advisory cycle.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track completed-deal fees, compensation, margins and valuation under a specified activity scenario.
claims.reason: This is a conditional exposure thesis, not a dated return target. Eisman discloses owning PJT.
claims.next_check: Track completed-deal fees, compensation, margins and valuation under a specified activity scenario.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare binding agreements and realized US net pricing with prior expectations.
claims.reason: Political demands are not the same as implemented net prices. The magnitude depends on product, program, volumes and negotiated terms.
claims.next_check: Compare binding agreements and realized US net pricing with prior expectations.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track volume, net pricing and share by geography and indication.
claims.reason: The operating thesis requires matched branded-prescription and compounded-product data; guidance cuts alone do not apportion the causes.
claims.next_check: Track volume, net pricing and share by geography and indication.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

evidence.title: Microsoft fiscal Q4 2025 results
evidence.finding: Revenue grew 18%, while Azure and other cloud services grew 39%. Aggregate growth is not an isolated return calculation on AI spending.

claims.next_check: Separate cloud revenue growth from capital intensity and cash returns.

claims.claim: Meta ad growth shows its large AI investments are paying off.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare monetization gains, operating costs, depreciation and incremental invested capital.
claims.reason: Revenue growth is real and consistent with better targeting and engagement, but it does not prove the incremental return on every AI project or future spending commitment.

evidence.title: Meta Q2 2025 results
evidence.finding: Revenue grew 22%. Ad impressions and pricing contributed to growth, but the release does not identify a counterfactual return on all incremental AI investment.

claims.next_check: Compare monetization gains, operating costs, depreciation and incremental invested capital.

claims.claim: Comcast broadband deterioration remains bad even if results beat depressed expectations.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track customer losses, pricing and cash generation independently of daily returns.
claims.reason: The issuer reports substantial broadband losses. A positive share reaction is compatible with a weak absolute operating result.

evidence.title: Comcast Q2 2025 results
evidence.finding: Domestic broadband customers fell 226,000, while mobile lines rose 378,000. Price movements do not erase the subscriber deterioration.

claims.next_check: Track customer losses, pricing and cash generation independently of daily returns.

claims.claim: Very high cable free-cash-flow yields imply the market expects the companies could go out of business.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Model future equity cash flow, debt obligations and required return.
claims.reason: A high current yield can also price declining cash flow, leverage, capital-spending normalization or a high required return without a bankruptcy outcome.
claims.next_check: Model future equity cash flow, debt obligations and required return.

assumptions: Positive current cash flow
Future cash flow and risk can differ from current conditions
proof.derivation: In a constant-growth valuation, cash-flow yield is approximately discount rate minus growth. A sufficiently low growth rate produces a high yield without setting future value to zero or assuming bankruptcy.

claims.next_check: Reconcile AWS growth, capex and forward operating-income guidance with prior expectations.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

claims.reason: This is a personal implementation rule, not a universal optimal-sizing result. Position size, uncertainty and loss capacity still matter.

review.title: Venture Capital Revealed: Behind the Schemes They Haven’t Told You
review.summary: Stu Ellman explains venture fund economics, concentrated winners, financing cycles and recapitalizations. Eisman draws out the distinction between unrealized marks and cash returns, and the risk of funding cash-burning companies with short runways. Ellman argues that large funds, AI and established managers are concentrating available capital. Later industry data support that concentration. Claims that markdowns require a new round are corrected by fair-value guidance and partly qualified within the conversation. Most forecasts and proposed AI or tokenization opportunities belong to Ellman, not Eisman.

framework_points: Separate DPI and realized cash from paper IRR.
Test how entry prices change a successful company’s contribution to fund returns.
Consider financing reserves and contractual priority alongside business quality.
Distinguish illiquid valuation judgment from permission to ignore deterioration.
Use recent deployment to identify active venture investors.

review.title: Tariffs Are Back, Apple’s Big Bet, and AI’s Real Impact - The Friday Market Wrap!
review.summary: Eisman distinguishes headline tariffs from effective rates, questions Apple spending promises, and surveys AI beneficiaries and potential victims. Gartner is his early example of AI threatening an incumbent information business. The wrap also contrasts current biotech earnings with pipeline news and reiterates skepticism about Opendoor.
review.assessment: The most consequential uncertainty is causal: Gartner weakness does not yet prove free AI substitution. Apple skepticism uses an inconsistent spending comparison because its US commitment includes suppliers, employees and content as well as physical investment. The pipeline discussion is useful if clinical outcomes are separated from investor expectations.
framework_points: Calculate effective policy exposure after exemptions.
Read the definition behind a large investment announcement.
Distinguish proprietary economics from commodity hardware.
Separate pipeline value from current earnings.
Look for both winners and threatened incumbents in AI.
transcript_cautions: Palantir tenfold growth is a reported CEO aspiration, not Eisman own target.
Apple US spending and China manufacturing investment are not automatically comparable categories.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

evidence.title: 2025 tariff requirements
evidence.finding: USMCA origin rules provide exemptions from specified tariffs, while sectoral Section 232 duties and other rules must be evaluated separately.

claims.next_check: Apply product-level origin rules and compare landed costs and realized relocation.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

evidence.finding: The original spending package included supplier purchases, direct employment, infrastructure, facilities and content production, rather than only new physical factory investment.

review.title: Steve Eisman Shares the Real Story Behind Predicting the 2008 Crash | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 20
review.summary: Melissa Lee probes Eisman’s long-term technology optimism, trade uncertainty and historical subprime research. His strongest framework is loan-vintage analysis, attention to documentation and retained risk, and separating a compelling thesis from timing. He remains bullish on US technology and expects more M&A, while disclosing Apple, other large technology, PJT, Apollo and Moody’s positions. The current macro explanations are less tightly evidenced. Claims that officials knew nothing about AIG before Lehman and that Apple manufactures entirely in China are contradicted by primary records; reserve-currency status also does not imply unlimited fiscal freedom.
review.assessment: Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.
review.speaker_map_notes: Melissa Lee interviews Steve Eisman. Lee’s questions and challenges are not counted as Eisman assertions; he explicitly adopts or rejects premises in his answers. Most substantive claims here are Eisman’s.
framework_points: Compare loan vintages at equal seasoning.
Wait for observable deterioration after forming a structural suspicion.
Study borrowing costs, execution and legal mechanics before changing instruments.
Distinguish aggregate growth from regional outcomes.
Assess bank capital separately from pre-crisis reputational narratives.
Keep conditional trade risks distinct from base-case forecasts.
tools_and_charts: Stock borrow fees and CDS contracts
Sector weights and adjusted technology classification
transcript_cautions: Opening montage repeats later interview content.
The early phrase captioned long time ago is clarified immediately by repeated long-term bullish language.
Recording references early-August jobs data and the already recorded venture interview; publication is August 11.

Tarullo’s title and dates are misremembered: official biography says Board service January 2009-April 2017 and supervision committee chair. This is a supporting chronology caution, not a principal investment verdict.
Household’s specific rate illustration and some old bankruptcy/position claims are retrospective and lack trade records.
Company-name caption errors include Providian, Comerica, Norfolk Southern and New Century.
