claims.claim: Requesting a two-way market helps test whether a dealer valuation is executable.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Require firm size, validity period and matching contract terms.
claims.reason: A mark is an estimate; a firm bid and offer show the prices at which the dealer will transact for specified size and terms. Wide spreads can be informative without proving fraud.
claims.next_check: Require firm size, validity period and matching contract terms.

assumptions: A two-way quote is firm and applies to the same instrument and size.
proof.derivation: The bid and offer identify executable sale and purchase terms; an isolated valuation does not supply those terms.

claims.claim: FrontPoint risk managers, not Morgan Stanley staff, asked the team to reduce its positions.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect contemporaneous risk correspondence and governance.
claims.reason: This corrects the film narrative but remains personal recollection without inspected risk records.
claims.next_check: Inspect contemporaneous risk correspondence and governance.

claims.claim: Meeting counterparties and issuers was intended to test whether the short thesis was wrong.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Document the strongest opposing evidence and how it changed the thesis.
claims.reason: This is a research principle and recollection; the desired practice is to seek disconfirmation rather than count meetings as proof.
claims.next_check: Document the strongest opposing evidence and how it changed the thesis.

claims.claim: He told Option One that subprime losses would not stop at 5%.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.horizon: Historical 2007 statement, no precise horizon reproduced
claims.test: Recover the contemporaneous statement, portfolio and realized loss series.
claims.reason: This is a retrospective quoted call with an unspecified pool and loss denominator. The audit cannot turn it into a new 2025 forecast or a precise verified historical return.
claims.next_check: Recover the contemporaneous statement, portfolio and realized loss series.

claims.claim: By August 2007 he considered the mortgage market collapse evident in lenders and derivative prices.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare dated market series and contemporaneous records.
claims.reason: The broad deterioration is documented, but his recognition date and portfolio marks are personal recollections.
claims.next_check: Compare dated market series and contemporaneous records.

claims.claim: Morgan Stanley proprietary mortgage exposure produced roughly $10 billion of losses in late 2007.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use the disclosed categories and dates.
claims.reason: The issuer reported $9.4 billion Q4 mortgage-related writedowns, including $7.8 billion US subprime trading positions. Roughly $10 billion is a reasonable rounded recollection, but this was not every bank exposure.

evidence.title: Q4 and full-year 2007 results
evidence.finding: Morgan Stanley reported $9.4 billion mortgage-related Q4 writedowns, including $7.8 billion US subprime trading positions. This supports the large-loss recollection, with the exact amount and reporting period corrected.

claims.next_check: Use the disclosed categories and dates.

claims.claim: A gain on a bilateral derivative means an offsetting contractual loss for the other side.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Trace hedges, collateral and counterparty exposure.
claims.reason: Before fees, defaults and other positions, the two sides of the same contract have opposite cash flows. A counterparty may hedge elsewhere, so this does not identify its net firm loss.
claims.next_check: Trace hedges, collateral and counterparty exposure.

assumptions: One bilateral contract, excluding fees and counterparty failure.
proof.derivation: Every contractual payment from one side is the receipt of the other; their net transfer sums to zero.

claims.claim: The absence of visible loss reports despite profitable shorts prompted him to investigate who held the offsetting exposure.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Map economic exposure across intermediaries and hedge books.
claims.reason: This is a useful investigative question and personal history, not proof that every missing mark was fraudulent.
claims.next_check: Map economic exposure across intermediaries and hedge books.

claims.claim: Bear Stearns failure involved inability to roll funding and emergency support around its sale to JPMorgan.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Distinguish short-term liquidity, asset losses and rescue terms.
claims.reason: The official crisis investigation documents the funding run and rescue. This is a historical explanation, not a fresh collapse forecast.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13
evidence.finding: Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

claims.next_check: Distinguish short-term liquidity, asset losses and rescue terms.

claims.claim: The mortgage-security system turned a useful financing mechanism into a source of fraud and systemic damage.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate demonstrated misconduct from design flaws, leverage and policy failures.
claims.reason: Investigations document fraud, underwriting failures and institutional incentives. The broad moral summary cannot replace institution-specific findings or exclude other causes.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13
evidence.finding: Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

claims.next_check: Separate demonstrated misconduct from design flaws, leverage and policy failures.

claims.claim: No major modern investment bank had failed except because of fraud.
claims.speaker: Mike Mayo, as recalled by Eisman
claims.test: Specify institutions, dates and definitions of failure and fraud.
claims.reason: This is Mike Mayo reported statement, followed by Eisman skeptical reply. The universe and period are undefined, and it is not Eisman endorsed historical rule.
claims.next_check: Specify institutions, dates and definitions of failure and fraud.

claims.claim: Issuer-paid ratings and the threat of business moving to a competitor compromised rating quality.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect rating communications, model changes and business incentives.
claims.reason: The investigative record supports conflicts and failures. The film meeting dialogue is illustrative, not a verbatim official record.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13
evidence.finding: Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

claims.next_check: Inspect rating communications, model changes and business incentives.

claims.claim: Moody management considered its ratings sound after an initial downgrade, while the team strongly disagreed.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Locate contemporaneous meeting notes and rating actions.
claims.reason: The meeting content and exact downgrade date are recollections not independently verified here.
claims.next_check: Locate contemporaneous meeting notes and rating actions.

claims.claim: The film dramatizes the decision to close the shorts; he cannot recall the exact actual closing date.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use original transaction records for performance analysis.
claims.reason: The explicit uncertainty prevents reconstructing a precise trade exit or investment return from this episode.
claims.next_check: Use original transaction records for performance analysis.

claims.claim: The team feared that systemic collapse could overwhelm even a successful short thesis.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Stress collateral access, liquidity and counterparty survival alongside asset value.
claims.reason: This retrospective fear illustrates counterparty and system risk but is not a new prediction.
claims.next_check: Stress collateral access, liquidity and counterparty survival alongside asset value.

claims.claim: Ordinary households bear substantial costs when financial-system failures become economic crises.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Measure distributional losses as well as financial-institution outcomes.
claims.reason: The official inquiry documents foreclosures, employment and wealth destruction. The universal rhetorical always is not treated as a literal exhaustive allocation of every loss.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13
evidence.finding: Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

claims.next_check: Measure distributional losses as well as financial-institution outcomes.

review.title: The Wild West of Crypto: Chaos, Shenanigans, & The AI Revolution | The Friday Market Wrap!
review.summary: The September 26 wrap connects opaque crypto leverage with fragile market plumbing, maps the AI investment chain and focuses on funding risk behind giant cloud commitments. Eisman warns about vendor financing while explicitly declining to predict a recession.
review.assessment: The most useful contribution is following the funding chain from customers to suppliers, rather than accepting backlog as cash. Several supporting statements overreach: Binance publishes leverage limits, Nvidia announced a staged letter of intent, Mitsubishi competes in turbines, and solar incentives were curtailed rather than universally erased.
framework_points: Trace financing and counterparties behind growth.
Inspect leverage and liquidation mechanisms.
Map chips, networks, power, cooling and applications separately.
Check thesis creep before reacting to recession fears.
transcript_cautions: He explicitly says he does not currently expect recession.
Reported Morgan Stanley spending forecasts are guest research, not an independently modeled Eisman forecast.
Apple installed base refers to devices, not necessarily distinct people.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.claim: Opaque leverage and weak regulation can amplify financial-market instability, as in the historical crash analogy.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare actual leverage, margin and liquidity structures rather than surface similarity.
claims.reason: The analogy identifies a mechanism but does not establish a repetition of 1929 or a dated crash forecast.
claims.next_check: Compare actual leverage, margin and liquidity structures rather than surface similarity.

claims.claim: Binance offers opaque high leverage without meaningful restrictions or publicly knowable limits.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate maximum permitted leverage from actual aggregate exposure.
claims.reason: High leverage and liquidation mechanics are real, but Binance publishes brackets and account restrictions. Aggregate customer leverage may remain opaque, which is different from no rules.

evidence.title: Futures leverage and margin rules
evidence.finding: The exchange publishes leverage brackets, maintenance margins and liquidation rules, including dated 2025 account restrictions. High leverage is real, but a claim that no limits or public information exist is false.

claims.next_check: Separate maximum permitted leverage from actual aggregate exposure.

claims.claim: Forced Ether liquidations on overseas exchanges caused the entire Monday crypto selloff.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Reconstruct exchange liquidations, timing, depth and competing catalysts.
claims.reason: The narrative lacks inspected event-level positions and flows sufficient to attribute the whole move.
claims.next_check: Reconstruct exchange liquidations, timing, depth and competing catalysts.

claims.claim: Intermediary and reserve-management risks can matter as much as the digital asset itself.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Analyze the full issuer, exchange, custodian and redemption chain.
claims.reason: Circle historical bank exposure and Tether reserve disclosures demonstrate distinct custody, liquidity and asset-composition risks.

evidence.title: USDC reserve risk and de-peg
evidence.finding: Circle acknowledged a USDC de-peg during the SVB episode and a $3.3 billion bank deposit exposure. Pegs and short-duration reserves are not a guarantee of constant market prices.

evidence.title: Reserve assurance report
evidence.finding: The report is assurance on a specified reserves report under ISAE 3000, not a full financial-statement audit. Disclosed reserves include non-Treasury assets.

claims.next_check: Analyze the full issuer, exchange, custodian and redemption chain.

claims.claim: Tether non-Treasury assets create a potential stablecoin contagion risk.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Stress liquidity and capital against redemption scenarios.
claims.reason: The assets exist, but a future de-peg and damage to Circle require a stress event. Calling Tether unregulated also overlooks its Salvadoran license.

evidence.title: Reserve assurance report
evidence.finding: The report is assurance on a specified reserves report under ISAE 3000, not a full financial-statement audit. Disclosed reserves include non-Treasury assets.

evidence.title: El Salvador issuer license
evidence.finding: Tether announced a Salvadoran stablecoin-issuer and digital-asset-service license. Not being a US-regulated issuer is different from having no regulation.

claims.next_check: Stress liquidity and capital against redemption scenarios.

claims.claim: Only stablecoins can achieve a meaningful role in global payments.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Distinguish the unit of account, transfer rail and final settlement asset.
claims.reason: The categorical exclusion does not follow from volatility: conversion services can transfer other assets while quoting stable units. Commercial suitability remains a separate question.
claims.next_check: Distinguish the unit of account, transfer rail and final settlement asset.

assumptions: Conversion can occur at both ends of a transfer.
proof.proof: A volatile bridge asset can carry value between two stable-currency endpoints. Volatility imposes risk and cost but does not logically exclude meaningful payment use.
proof.derivation: A volatile bridge asset can carry value between two stable-currency endpoints. Volatility imposes risk and cost but does not logically exclude meaningful payment use.

claims.claim: Narrowing breadth makes the market feel tired and is unhealthy over time.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Specify breadth universe, calculation and forward-return test.
claims.reason: The impression and health criterion lack a return horizon or measurable failure threshold. A stated breadth snapshot is not a sell signal by itself.
claims.next_check: Specify breadth universe, calculation and forward-return test.

claims.claim: Technology leadership changes across successive investment waves, so current winners need not remain leaders.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Build point-in-time market-cap rankings with consistent classifications.
claims.reason: The principle is useful, but his 20-25% turnover estimate needs a consistent universe and historical constituent series. Visa and Mastercard classification also complicates a technology-only ranking.
claims.next_check: Build point-in-time market-cap rankings with consistent classifications.

claims.claim: Explosive token processing indicates growing demand for AI compute.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track unit costs, model mix and revenue per task as well as token volume.
claims.reason: Microsoft reported more than 100 trillion tokens, up fivefold, in fiscal Q3 2025. Token counts are not standardized measures of revenue, FLOPs or profitability across models.

evidence.title: Microsoft fiscal Q3 2025 earnings call
evidence.finding: Microsoft reported processing more than 100 trillion tokens in the quarter, up fivefold. The figure was a usage measure, not an equal multiple of revenue or profit.

claims.next_check: Track unit costs, model mix and revenue per task as well as token volume.

claims.claim: The AI buildout benefits chips, networking, data centers and selected data-analysis software.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Translate each link in the chain into issuer-level cash flows.
claims.reason: The exposure map is plausible, but individual stock winners depend on competitive share, margins, capex and price paid.
claims.next_check: Translate each link in the chain into issuer-level cash flows.

claims.claim: Only very large companies can finance hyperscale AI infrastructure.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare project equity, debt, contracts and partner funding.
claims.reason: Large project costs favor scale, but consortia, project finance and leasing can broaden participation. No minimum size is specified.
claims.next_check: Compare project equity, debt, contracts and partner funding.

claims.claim: Solar and wind are no longer part of the near-term power story because their incentives were removed.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect project start and in-service dates, credit rules and actual construction.
claims.reason: The policy accelerated deadlines and imposed conditions, but did not instantly eliminate every eligible project or all commercial demand. The broad exclusion is too categorical.

evidence.title: Clean electricity credits after the 2025 law
evidence.finding: Wind and solar termination rules include construction-start and placed-in-service exceptions. The final law is not identical to every June proposal and does not terminate every project credit on one date.

claims.next_check: Inspect project start and in-service dates, credit rules and actual construction.

claims.claim: Gas-turbine scarcity and rising construction costs support the equipment opportunity.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track orders, capacity, contract prices and project conversion.
claims.reason: Mitsubishi disclosures confirm substantial large-frame turbine orders and market share. The mechanism is stronger than the claim of only two suppliers.

evidence.title: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries fiscal 2024 results presentation
evidence.finding: MHI disclosed 25 large-frame gas turbine orders and substantial global market share, establishing a major supplier beyond GE and Siemens.

claims.next_check: Track orders, capacity, contract prices and project conversion.

claims.claim: Only GE Vernova and Siemens make large gas turbines.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Include all large-frame suppliers in the market model.
claims.reason: Mitsubishi is another major supplier, directly contradicting the duopoly premise.

evidence.title: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries fiscal 2024 results presentation
evidence.finding: MHI disclosed 25 large-frame gas turbine orders and substantial global market share, establishing a major supplier beyond GE and Siemens.

claims.next_check: Include all large-frame suppliers in the market model.

claims.claim: Nuclear, uranium and grid construction could benefit from rising data-center electricity demand.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Model contract timing, regulation, construction costs and valuation.
claims.reason: The theme has no return horizon or price discipline. Demand does not remove licensing, construction and financing constraints.
claims.next_check: Model contract timing, regulation, construction costs and valuation.

claims.claim: Oklo is highly speculative and could supply data-center power if its reactors obtain approval.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track licensing, construction, fuel availability and commercial operation.
claims.reason: The conditional commercial deployment is a multi-year project, not established by a stock rally or an early agreement.
claims.next_check: Track licensing, construction, fuel availability and commercial operation.

claims.claim: Electrical equipment and cooling are additional ways to participate in AI capital spending.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track equipment backlogs, book-to-bill and cash generation.
claims.reason: This is an exposure map without an expected-return target. Supplier margins, order conversion and valuation remain essential.
claims.next_check: Track equipment backlogs, book-to-bill and cash generation.

claims.claim: Apple will lag until it presents a clearer AI strategy, while its installed base gives it bargaining power.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Define the strategy milestone and compare adoption, economics and total returns.
claims.reason: Until clarity is a subjective trigger with no benchmark or end date. The 2.4 billion base refers to devices rather than unique people, and public AI products already existed.
claims.next_check: Define the strategy milestone and compare adoption, economics and total returns.

claims.claim: AI threatens consulting and software moats, but incumbents may adapt and should not yet be written off.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track retention, pricing, AI product adoption and actual replacement.
claims.reason: He explicitly preserves the adaptation possibility. Falling share prices alone do not demonstrate customer substitution or moat destruction.
claims.next_check: Track retention, pricing, AI product adoption and actual replacement.

claims.claim: A recession could impair private AI fundraising and cause Oracle to miss its five-year revenue path.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track funding access and contract conversion under a defined recession scenario.
claims.reason: The 2030 path is unfinished and recession is a condition, not a prediction he says is currently likely. Funding may also come from customers, partners or operating cash.

evidence.title: Oracle fiscal Q1 2026 results
evidence.finding: RPO rose 359% to $455 billion; recognized quarterly revenue was $14.9 billion, up 12%, and cloud infrastructure revenue grew 55%. Backlog is not current realized revenue.

claims.next_check: Track funding access and contract conversion under a defined recession scenario.

claims.claim: OpenAI accounts for about $300 billion of Oracle backlog and cannot currently fund all of it from cash on hand.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect contract terms, maturity schedules and customer financial disclosures.
claims.reason: The concentration figure is attributed to others digging into the numbers. The public Oracle release does not itself identify every counterparty or payment schedule, so the exact concentration is not independently verified here.
claims.next_check: Inspect contract terms, maturity schedules and customer financial disclosures.

claims.claim: Nvidia announced a $100 billion OpenAI investment, showing ready access to huge funding.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate intentions, definitive commitments and disbursements.
claims.reason: The announcement was a letter of intent for up to $100 billion in staged investments, not cash already received. It supports proposed access, subject to execution.

evidence.title: OpenAI strategic partnership letter of intent
evidence.finding: The announcement was a letter of intent, with proposed investment up to $100 billion in stages as infrastructure deployed. It was not $100 billion of cash already transferred.

claims.next_check: Separate intentions, definitive commitments and disbursements.

claims.claim: Sovereign investors and capacity-backstop agreements are widening the funding and demand base.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track signed terms, funded amounts and actual purchased capacity.
claims.reason: Announcements do not establish that all financing closed or that capacity is economically utilized.
claims.next_check: Track signed terms, funded amounts and actual purchased capacity.

claims.claim: Supplier financing of customers makes AI demand less independent and creates circularity risk.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Trace external end-customer cash, contractual obligations and related-party exposure.
claims.reason: Nvidia proposed funding a customer that would deploy Nvidia systems. This creates correlated supplier-customer exposure without proving fictitious revenue or inevitable collapse.

evidence.title: OpenAI strategic partnership letter of intent
evidence.finding: The announcement was a letter of intent, with proposed investment up to $100 billion in stages as infrastructure deployed. It was not $100 billion of cash already transferred.

claims.next_check: Trace external end-customer cash, contractual obligations and related-party exposure.

claims.claim: Morgan Stanley projects $2.9 trillion data-center spending through 2028, roughly half funded by hyperscaler cash flow.
claims.speaker: Morgan Stanley, reported by Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare the dated forecast scope with realized expenditures and funding.
claims.reason: This is identified as outside research and the 2028 horizon is incomplete. It is not an Eisman-generated forecast.
claims.next_check: Compare the dated forecast scope with realized expenditures and funding.

claims.claim: Today financial-system resilience means the next recession should be ordinary rather than another GFC.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Specify stress losses, leverage, liquidity and failure thresholds across the system.
claims.reason: The forecast has no date and ordinary is undefined. Confidence in banks does not rule out losses in other institutions or market plumbing.
claims.next_check: Specify stress losses, leverage, liquidity and failure thresholds across the system.

claims.claim: During recession fears, review thesis failures and taxes rather than automatically liquidate the whole portfolio.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare after-tax outcomes and drawdowns under a defined mandate.
claims.reason: This is a portfolio-management preference, conditional on risk tolerance and liquidity needs. It is not a guaranteed optimal action for everyone.
claims.next_check: Compare after-tax outcomes and drawdowns under a defined mandate.

claims.claim: Monthly consumer securitization credit data can reveal deterioration earlier than slower aggregate reports.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare delinquencies, losses and macro outcomes using information available at each date.
claims.reason: Frequency helps timeliness but leading predictive value requires out-of-sample testing and adjustments for loan vintage and borrower mix.
claims.next_check: Compare delinquencies, losses and macro outcomes using information available at each date.

claims.claim: Too little regulation invites abusive risk taking, while excessive regulation suppresses productive activity.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Evaluate specific rules, externalities and observed costs.
claims.reason: The claim supplies neither a calibrated optimum nor a measurable threshold for too much or too little.
claims.next_check: Evaluate specific rules, externalities and observed costs.

review.title: The AI Revolution: Winners, Losers, & The Future of Tech | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 27

metadata.title: The AI Revolution: Winners, Losers, & The Future of Tech | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 27

review.summary: Dan Ives offers a broad AI bull case spanning identity, infrastructure, Apple distribution, Tesla autonomy, Palantir and small nuclear reactors. Eisman repeatedly probes adoption, operating proof, timing, interim earnings and China risk. Most precise operating visions extend to 2027-2032 and remain open; the xAI investment direction happened later than the specified November 2025 date. Important guest premises on European zero adoption and Palantir having no sales force are contradicted by primary evidence.
review.assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Dan Ives. Most specific technology and price forecasts are Ives; Eisman often questions rather than endorses them.
framework_points: Separate revolutionary technology from winners and losers.
Ask whether an incumbent moat protects renewals or merely historical profits.
Differentiate earnings forecasts from stock-price forecasts.
Demand operating and regulatory milestones for pre-revenue technology.
Identify how network utility actually accrues to token holders.
Trace second-order beneficiaries while checking their distinct economics.
tools_and_charts: AI capex and aggregate cash comparison
transcript_cautions: Opening montage duplicates later claims.
Publication is September 29, but discussion of the September 8 Eightco announcement as this week implies earlier recording; exact recording date not established.
Captions garble Eightco, Oklo, Palantir and decimal stock prices.
Perplexity/Google references appear confused; do not infer a verified ownership relationship.
Ives discloses chairmanship/ETF interests; promotional exposure is relevant context.
Guest forecasts are not Eisman forecasts.

claims.claim: Eisman and Ives are bullish on the market.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.
claims.qualifications: No benchmark, horizon or expected return is specified.
claims.reason: The statement does not specify an objective threshold, horizon or counterfactual that permits a determinate outcome grade.
claims.next_check: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

claims.claim: Eightco's Worldcoin treasury announcement and Ives appointment sparked an extraordinary stock move after a large private placement.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.
claims.reason: Financing and appointment are verified. Exact event returns are not independently verified; captions lose the decimal in the $1.46 financing price.

evidence.title: Eightco Worldcoin treasury private placement
evidence.finding: Announced $250 million placement at $1.46 per share plus $20 million BitMine strategic investment, with Dan Ives chairman. Transcript decimal rendering should not be read as $145.

claims.next_check: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

claims.claim: World's proof-of-human network will become essential in an AI/bot world and grow from about 15 million verified users to 100 million in the next year, eventually billions.
claims.speaker: Dan Ives
claims.horizon: approximately September 2026 for 100 million; eventual billions
claims.test: Obtain September 2026 verified-human count, separating app downloads, accounts, verifications and credential uses.
claims.reason: The one-year horizon has elapsed. June 2026 official count was only over 18 million, but no complete deadline count was inspected, so the target remains unresolved rather than too early or conclusively wrong.

evidence.title: The Simple Plan: Phase 3 of the Real Human Network
evidence.finding: Reports over 18 million verified humans and more than 450 million uses of World ID. This is far below the guest's 100 million target but precedes its September 2026 deadline and is not final deadline evidence.

claims.next_check: Obtain September 2026 verified-human count, separating app downloads, accounts, verifications and credential uses.

claims.claim: Orb scanning transfers encrypted identity information to the user's app and deletes it from the device, providing private authentication.
claims.speaker: Dan Ives
claims.test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.
claims.reason: Privacy, retention, encryption and backup behavior were not checked against the original architecture and current policy.
claims.next_check: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

claims.claim: Advertising and social-media authentication fees will generate network value that supports Worldcoin and Eightco's token treasury strategy.
claims.speaker: Dan Ives
claims.test: Trace actual fee flows, token demand/supply and treasury NAV per share rather than using user growth alone.
claims.qualifications: Network utility does not automatically accrue to token holders or treasury shareholders; token economics, dilution and legal rights matter.
claims.reason: The stated future horizon or conditional scenario remains unfinished at the 2026-11-10 cutoff.
claims.next_check: Trace actual fee flows, token demand/supply and treasury NAV per share rather than using user growth alone.

claims.claim: AI is an industrial revolution with a tech bull market lasting at least two or three more years as enterprise spending expands into consumer use.
claims.speaker: Dan Ives
claims.test: Track technology-sector total returns, valuation and earnings through the stated multiyear horizon.
claims.reason: The stated future horizon or conditional scenario remains unfinished at the 2026-11-10 cutoff.
claims.next_check: Track technology-sector total returns, valuation and earnings through the stated multiyear horizon.

claims.claim: Infrastructure suppliers including NVIDIA and CoreWeave are the obvious current AI winners, while the revolution will also produce losers.

review.title: U.S. Consumers Are Collapsing: Cars, Credit, & the Chaos Ahead | The Weekly Wrap
review.summary: Eisman interviews Lakshmi Ganapathy about stressed consumers, auto credit and Opendoor. The conversation argues that pandemic support inflated apparent credit quality and that weak borrowers face a renewed cash-flow squeeze, before criticizing speculative enthusiasm for an unproven housing model.
review.assessment: Some stress was real, but the broad collapse narrative overstates the evidence: later card delinquency flows eased and CarMax sales recovered. Eisman makes a clear macro accounting error by subtracting the entire AI capex level from GDP growth, and an incorrect categorical claim about student-loan bankruptcy. Many allegations about hidden delinquencies and defective homes remain unsupported.
framework_points: Inspect borrower cash flow and vintage quality.
Distinguish reported credit scores from underlying capacity to repay.
Test business unit economics before accepting a meme narrative.
Separate a weak consumer segment from the whole economy.
transcript_cautions: The guest is Lakshmi Ganapathy of Unicus Research; automatic captions misspell her name.
Statements alleging concealed delinquencies, channel pressure or defective homes are assertions, not established findings.
The 76,000 repossession caption is inconsistent with the adjacent 2.42 million and 30% figures; exact counts are not scored without audio verification.
The guest later clarifies that the firm does not trade its published recommendations; historical recommendation performance is not audited personal trading performance.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman hosts; Lakshmi Ganapathy supplies most consumer, auto and Opendoor assertions. Host summaries are labeled as adopted, exploratory or conditional rather than automatically attributing the entire guest case to him.

claims.claim: Subtracting about $400 billion of AI capex from about $530 billion of GDP growth shows less than 0.5% growth outside AI.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use BEA real contribution accounts and domestic incremental investment.
claims.reason: The calculation subtracts a spending level from a change, mixes nominal GDP with a real growth estimate and ignores imports, domestic value added and the prior-year spending base. It does not estimate the contribution to growth.
claims.next_check: Use BEA real contribution accounts and domestic incremental investment.

assumptions: GDP growth is a change between periods; gross capex is a level and may include imports.
proof.proof: Even unchanged annual capex of $400 billion would add zero direct incremental spending growth. Subtracting its full level from GDP growth wrongly attributes the existing base to new growth; nominal and real measures also require consistent prices.
proof.derivation: Even unchanged annual capex of $400 billion would add zero direct incremental spending growth. Subtracting its full level from GDP growth wrongly attributes the existing base to new growth; nominal and real measures also require consistent prices.

claims.speaker: Lakshmi Ganapathy
claims.test: Separate transfers, debt payment, forbearance and each reporting program.
claims.reason: Student-loan reporting changes materially affected credit scores, but that does not establish that all consumer health was an illusion or that credit-card delinquencies universally stopped being reported.

evidence.title: Student-loan delinquencies and credit scores
evidence.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
evidence.finding: More than 2.2 million newly delinquent borrowers lost over 100 points and more than one million lost at least 150 points. Impacts varied by initial score; this does not mean every borrower lost 200-250 points.

claims.next_check: Separate transfers, debt payment, forbearance and each reporting program.

metadata.title: Inside the AI Chip War: From Nvidia’s Dominance to Intel’s Turmoil | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 28

review.summary: Stacy Rasgon separates the AI semiconductor boom from the weaker analog cycle, stresses NVIDIA's software ecosystem, and remains cautious about AMD and Intel. Eisman tests funding and return assumptions without declaring AI useless or predicting an imminent collapse. The clearest direct correction is that the announced NVIDIA investment in OpenAI was staged. The guest's claim that outsiders do not use TPUs is contradicted by Google's documented multi-year Anthropic relationship.
review.assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Stacy Rasgon. Most sector calls belong to Rasgon; Eisman probes returns and valuation and accepts the staged-investment correction.
framework_points: Distinguish economic usefulness from returns on invested capital.
Separate cyclic digestion from a failed structural thesis.
Treat capex cuts as potentially late signals and monitor underlying use.
Do not infer equity value from TAM times assumed share.
Distinguish liquidity support from operating competitiveness.
Demand differentiated customer preference rather than a second-source narrative.
tools_and_charts: GPU versus ASIC share and workload economics
TI inventory days and backlog visibility
Intel foundry losses and external customer milestones
transcript_cautions: Opening montage duplicates later discussion.
All 2009 caption lines were read, including a reread of an initially truncated middle segment.
Guest numbers and management targets are not automatically Eisman forecasts.
Transcript occasionally garbles chip names and semiconductor terms.
The guest immediately self-corrects the lithography size direction; it is not a substantive mistaken thesis.

review.summary: The October 10 mailbag gives space to a developer skeptical of workplace AI adoption, then discusses youth employment, housing savings, retirement allocation and Apple. Eisman insists that AI investment eventually needs an economic return, while offering several broad personal-finance judgments.
review.assessment: The skepticism about usage metrics is a useful hypothesis, not evidence that all AI is unproductive. The repeated GDP arithmetic is wrong. His retirement advice also compares a tax rate on gains with an annual bond yield too crudely and omits important RMD cohort and Roth distinctions.
framework_points: Measure outcomes rather than tool usage alone.
Require economic returns on capital spending.
Learn enough finance to question model answers.
Include taxes, liquidity and transaction costs in allocation decisions.
transcript_cautions: Max is an unidentified listener whose workplace account is not independently verified. It is not automatically Eisman testimony.
The wrap was recorded before the later Friday tariff-market reversal and should not be treated as describing every event that calendar day.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.claim: The administration will encourage a wave of regional-bank mergers after the announced Fifth Third-Comerica deal.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track completed transactions, approval times and deal value against prior cycles.
claims.reason: The forecast has no deal-volume threshold or time horizon. Announcement is not completed acquisition.
claims.next_check: Track completed transactions, approval times and deal value against prior cycles.

claims.claim: Subtracting about $400 billion of AI capex from about $530 billion of GDP growth shows less than 0.5% growth outside AI.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use BEA real contribution accounts and domestic incremental investment.
claims.reason: The calculation subtracts a spending level from a change, mixes nominal GDP with a real growth estimate and ignores imports, domestic value added and the prior-year spending base. It does not estimate the contribution to growth.
claims.next_check: Use BEA real contribution accounts and domestic incremental investment.

assumptions: GDP growth is a change between periods; gross capex is a level and may include imports.
proof.proof: Even unchanged annual capex of $400 billion would add zero direct incremental spending growth. Subtracting its full level from GDP growth wrongly attributes the existing base to new growth; nominal and real measures also require consistent prices.
proof.derivation: Even unchanged annual capex of $400 billion would add zero direct incremental spending growth. Subtracting its full level from GDP growth wrongly attributes the existing base to new growth; nominal and real measures also require consistent prices.

claims.claim: AI capital spending eventually needs strong economic returns to justify investment and stock valuations.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Model incremental cash flows, reinvestment and financing cost.
claims.reason: Capital creates value only when discounted future cash benefits justify the resources committed. A rising stock or usage count alone is insufficient.
claims.next_check: Model incremental cash flows, reinvestment and financing cost.

assumptions: Evaluate the investment economically using discounted incremental cash flows.
proof.proof: Net present value equals discounted incremental net cash flows minus investment. Positive spending or adoption alone cannot establish positive NPV.
proof.derivation: Net present value equals discounted incremental net cash flows minus investment. Positive spending or adoption alone cannot establish positive NPV.

claims.next_check: Compare usage, delivery time, defect rates and customer outcomes.

claims.next_check: Specify after-tax real returns, volatility, drawdowns and horizon.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

claims.next_check: Specify region, purchase price, rent alternative and long-run real total return.

claims.claim: Housing decisions should include tax, insurance, maintenance, transaction costs and the possibility that renting is better.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

claims.next_check: Build a matched after-tax rent-versus-buy cash-flow comparison.

assumptions: Both housing choices provide consumption value and generate different cash flows.
proof.proof: Total ownership cost includes financing, taxes, insurance, upkeep and transaction costs less sale proceeds. Omitting any material term biases a comparison with rent.
proof.derivation: Total ownership cost includes financing, taxes, insurance, upkeep and transaction costs less sale proceeds. Omitting any material term biases a comparison with rent.

claims.claim: Matching realized stock gains and losses can reduce the current capital-gains tax bill.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Apply actual basis, realized gains, losses and wash-sale restrictions.
claims.reason: IRS investment-income rules provide capital-loss offsets, subject to netting, holding-period and wash-sale rules.

evidence.title: Publication 550 (2025): Constructive Sales
evidence.finding: Shorting the same appreciated stock generally creates a taxable constructive sale. The closed-transaction exception requires close by 30 days after tax-year-end, 60 days continued ownership and no reduction of risk during those 60 days.

claims.next_check: Apply actual basis, realized gains, losses and wash-sale restrictions.

claims.claim: Learning finance directly remains valuable because knowing an answer is different from understanding and checking it.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Test ability to explain assumptions, detect errors and apply concepts independently.
claims.reason: This is an educational principle rather than a measurable forecast about credential returns. He describes his own Level I experience.
claims.next_check: Test ability to explain assumptions, detect errors and apply concepts independently.

claims.claim: Paying roughly 30% capital-gains tax to buy a 6% bond fund is inherently bad mathematics.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare complete after-tax future cash flows under both allocations.
claims.reason: The tax applies to taxable gains, not necessarily all sale proceeds, while yield is an annual rate. Comparing these percentages alone ignores basis, holding period, future tax, risk and liabilities.
claims.next_check: Compare complete after-tax future cash flows under both allocations.

assumptions: A $100 position has $80 basis and a 30% tax rate on gains.
proof.proof: Selling generates tax of 0.30*(100-80)=$6, not $30. A one-time $6 cost cannot be compared directly with a 6% annual yield without horizon and risk assumptions.
proof.derivation: Selling generates tax of 0.30*(100-80)=$6, not $30. A one-time $6 cost cannot be compared directly with a 6% annual yield without horizon and risk assumptions.

claims.claim: IRA owners must begin withdrawals at 73, and those distributions are a way to buy safer bonds in retirement.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Identify account type, birth year, basis, liquidity needs and allocation before applying the rule.
claims.reason: Age 73 applies to specified cohorts, while later cohorts begin at 75 and Roth owners have no lifetime RMD. The allocation idea is optional; investors need not wait for distributions to change holdings inside an account.

evidence.title: Applicable RMD ages and Roth accounts
evidence.finding: The applicable RMD age is 73 for specified birth cohorts and 75 for later cohorts. Designated Roth accounts are exempt from owner lifetime RMD requirements; distributions and internal asset trades are different events.

evidence.title: 2025 Form 5329 instructions
evidence.finding: Roth IRA owners have no lifetime required minimum distributions. Required ages and account types must be distinguished.

claims.next_check: Identify account type, birth year, basis, liquidity needs and allocation before applying the rule.

claims.claim: Apple China dependence was largely neutralized by a US-investment deal providing tariff exemption.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Map origin, components, assembly and each applicable tariff program.
claims.reason: The supply-chain exposure remains a strategic issue and exemptions under one tariff program do not remove every other duty. The broad all-products exemption explanation is too strong.

evidence.title: 2025 tariff requirements
evidence.finding: USMCA origin rules provide exemptions from specified tariffs, while sectoral Section 232 duties and other rules must be evaluated separately.

claims.next_check: Map origin, components, assembly and each applicable tariff program.

claims.claim: Google won its antitrust case and can continue lucrative payments to Apple.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate liability, payment terms and remedy restrictions.
claims.reason: The remedies avoided a blanket payment ban, but monopolization liability and restrictions survived. A profitable payment stream is not a complete legal victory.

evidence.title: Google search remedies
evidence.finding: The remedies included prohibitions on exclusive distribution contracts and mandatory data and syndication access. The monopolization liability finding remained; relief from a requested breakup was not complete victory in the case.

claims.next_check: Separate liability, payment terms and remedy restrictions.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare earnings revisions and explicit strategy developments with other factors.

claims.next_check: Compare earnings revisions and explicit strategy developments with other factors.

review.summary: Eisman expresses a modest turn toward concern about a bifurcated economy, consumer stress and AI returns. His headline subtraction of total AI capex from annual GDP growth is invalid growth accounting and should not support the ex-AI stagnation thesis. Liesman offers qualified tariff concerns, acknowledges near-term resilience exceeded his expectations, discusses Fed political context, and ends with historical reflections on Russia. The episode repeatedly separates conditional mechanisms from precisely timed forecasts.
review.assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews CNBC economics reporter Steve Liesman. Distinct host and guest claims are maintained; assent to a question does not transfer every guest forecast to Eisman.
framework_points: Separate markets, corporate margins and domestic output.
Use changes in domestic real investment when decomposing real GDP growth.
Test consumer stress across multiple credit and spending categories.
Evaluate policy forecasts under the policy actually specified.
Trace who captures technological returns and who finances the buildout.
Distinguish asset-price, employment and income-distribution channels.
tools_and_charts: GDP versus total AI capex arithmetic
transcript_cautions: Opening montage repeats the body.
All 1471 caption lines were read.
Steve Liesman is repeatedly rendered Leeman or Leaf in captions.
Market and GDP concern does not amount to an unconditional recession forecast.
The $500 to $1500-$2000 hotel-price example is explicitly made up.
Russia anecdotes and confidential market conversations are not independent empirical evidence.

review.title: The Bank Stock Rout: Facts vs Fiction | The Weekly Wrap
review.summary: The October 17 wrap uses bank earnings supplements to distinguish isolated commercial-credit problems from system-wide distress. It explains bank valuation through tangible returns, argues for a merger cycle and reiterates the value of efficient scale competitors such as Progressive.
review.assessment: His process of comparing institutions and sizing losses is stronger than a headline-driven crisis call. Yet he overstates the universality of 2009 capital raising and turns a preference for bank takeovers into an overly exclusive reason to own regionals. The future normal-cycle view remains contingent.
framework_points: Use earnings to test the original thesis.
Compare credit trends across banks and normalize losses by size.
Link bank valuation to sustainable tangible returns.
Distinguish a funding crisis from ordinary credit losses.
transcript_cautions: Captions use ROCE where the intended bank measure is ROTCE.
Fraud descriptions should be read as reported allegations or proceedings, not a finding against every associated borrower.
He ends by admitting he cannot yet decide the competing AI-productivity accounts.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.claim: The US-China trade story remains unsettled, though the parties will probably work it out.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Specify binding measures and an evaluation date.
claims.reason: Probably work it out has no defined agreement or horizon, and he explicitly expresses hope.
claims.next_check: Specify binding measures and an evaluation date.

claims.claim: Quarterly earnings should test the investment thesis, and holding is itself an active decision.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Write the thesis and disconfirming evidence before each reporting cycle.
claims.reason: This is his research discipline, not a claim that an unchanged thesis guarantees a good return.
claims.next_check: Write the thesis and disconfirming evidence before each reporting cycle.

claims.claim: Strong advisory and trading results suggest an M&A cycle benefiting Goldman, Morgan Stanley and boutiques.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track completed deal fees, margins, market share and valuation.
claims.reason: Current fee strength and a future massive wave are separate claims; the latter lacks a measurable duration and volume hurdle.
claims.next_check: Track completed deal fees, margins, market share and valuation.

claims.claim: Current bank disclosures do not show broad consumer credit collapse, and individual losses should be judged relative to bank size.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare standardized credit flows, loss absorption and borrower mix.
claims.reason: JPMorgan disclosures support substantial profitability and detailed credit monitoring, while household data later show uneven rather than uniform stress. This does not prove no problems anywhere outside the bank sample.

evidence.title: JPMorgan Q3 2025 financial supplement
evidence.finding: Net income was $14.393 billion and ROTCE 20%. The supplement provides detailed business-level credit, nonaccrual, capital and profitability data, allowing isolated losses to be compared with the balance sheet.

evidence.title: Household Debt Increased Moderately; Delinquency Transition Rates Remain Flat
evidence.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
evidence.finding: Official indexed release inspected; direct open failed. Q3 stock delinquency rose to 5.0%, but serious card transitions improved to 6.87% from 7.05% a year earlier; auto transitions 3.02% versus 2.99%. This is uneven stress, not a general new credit collapse.

claims.next_check: Compare standardized credit flows, loss absorption and borrower mix.

claims.claim: Commercial credit deterioration differs markedly across large banks.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare matching loan populations, nonaccrual policies and dates.
claims.reason: The comparison requires aligned definitions and complete supplements for every bank; the inspected JPMorgan file alone does not verify every quoted peer percentage.
claims.next_check: Compare matching loan populations, nonaccrual policies and dates.

claims.claim: Zions and Western Alliance issues appear isolated rather than evidence of immediate sector-wide failure.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Trace borrower connections, collateral and subsequent losses across lenders.
claims.reason: The word appear is appropriate, but absence of newly disclosed problems elsewhere cannot establish absence of all shared exposures.
claims.next_check: Trace borrower connections, collateral and subsequent losses across lenders.

claims.claim: Bank earnings supplements provide detailed evidence that can test a credit narrative.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Reconcile releases, supplements and regulatory filings.
claims.reason: The JPMorgan supplement supplies divisional results, nonaccruals, charge-offs and capital measures. Disclosure quality does not guarantee that every hidden exposure is known.

evidence.title: JPMorgan Q3 2025 financial supplement
evidence.finding: Net income was $14.393 billion and ROTCE 20%. The supplement provides detailed business-level credit, nonaccrual, capital and profitability data, allowing isolated losses to be compared with the balance sheet.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13
evidence.finding: Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

claims.next_check: Trace underwriting, funding and loss chronology.

evidence.title: JPMorgan Q3 2025 financial supplement
evidence.finding: Net income was $14.393 billion and ROTCE 20%. The supplement provides detailed business-level credit, nonaccrual, capital and profitability data, allowing isolated losses to be compared with the balance sheet.

claims.next_check: Compare normalized common earnings and average tangible equity, adjusting for risk.

claims.next_check: Compare sustainable returns, growth, risk and beginning multiples.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

claims.reason: The scale mechanism is plausible, but the relative contribution to deposit share and universal necessity to merge needs evidence.
claims.next_check: Compare cost ratios, deposit flows, technology spending and customer mix by size.

claims.claim: A supportive administration will produce a major regional-bank merger wave, making KRE attractive.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Define deal volume, valuation, financing and expected index total return.
claims.reason: A future wave has no threshold or time limit, and acquisition activity does not necessarily produce attractive index returns at any entry price.
claims.next_check: Define deal volume, valuation, financing and expected index total return.

claims.claim: First Horizon management acquisition ambitions undermined takeover expectations and hurt the group.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare call timing, peer news and changes in takeover probabilities.
claims.reason: A management comment can affect expectations, but the full stock and sector move is not causally isolated.
claims.next_check: Compare call timing, peer news and changes in takeover probabilities.

claims.claim: The only reason to own regional banks is a takeover, while CEOs resisting sales harm shareholders.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare standalone valuation and sale proceeds under explicit scenarios.
claims.reason: This is a strong investment preference, not a demonstrated universal truth. Standalone cash generation, capital returns and price can create other rationales.
claims.next_check: Compare standalone valuation and sale proceeds under explicit scenarios.

claims.claim: All banks were forced to raise dilutive capital in 2009, explaining their depressed long-run per-share paths.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate institution-specific dilution, splits and total return.
claims.reason: Dilution was important for some banks, but SCAP required additional equity at ten of nineteen assessed institutions, not all banks. Split adjustments and dividends also matter in return comparisons.

evidence.title: SCAP capital requirements
evidence.finding: Ten of nineteen assessed institutions were required to raise additional common equity. The requirement did not apply identically to every bank.

claims.next_check: Separate institution-specific dilution, splits and total return.

claims.claim: Efficient scale competitors can keep gaining share in mature industries by sharing cost advantages with customers.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track relative costs, customer prices, retention and share.
claims.reason: This is a conditional business-model framework, not proof that every named company always has the lowest cost or will keep winning.
claims.next_check: Track relative costs, customer prices, retention and share.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

claims.next_check: Track policy growth, combined ratio, pricing adequacy and valuation.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Seek representative task-level evidence rather than vote-count anecdotes.

review.summary: Craig Moffett and Michael Nathanson assess Apple, cable, wireless, advertising and streaming. The guests correctly anticipate a Google-based Siri partnership and the Paramount-Warner combination, while their cable equilibrium thesis remained unproven through the cutoff. Eisman discloses modest de-risking and repeats invalid GDP-minus-total-capex arithmetic. The closing discussion carefully distinguishes AI labor savings from the fraction suppliers can capture as profits.
review.assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman with Craig Moffett (telecom, cable and Apple) and Michael Nathanson (advertising and media). Speaker attribution is medium confidence for guest handoffs in unlabelled captions.
framework_points: Separate operating excellence from valuation.
Demand a catalyst and observable operating improvement for a cheap stock.
Check density, cost per passing and cost per connected customer before extrapolating infrastructure coverage.
Distinguish final customer demand from intercompany value-chain revenue.
Compare willingness to pay with competitive realized price.
Separate a successful transaction forecast from an alleged political motive.
tools_and_charts: Cable subscriber losses, mobile growth and conditional equilibrium
Fiber cost per connected home versus cable acquisition value
T-Mobile valuation and demographic subscriber bridge
Ad-share concentration and linear-TV household reach
Final AI revenue versus capex and labor savings

metadata.title: Inside the Data Center Boom: Understanding the Massive Infrastructure That Supports AI

review.summary: Nick Del Deo explains the distinct economics of data-center property, interconnection hubs, GPU clouds and fiber. The strongest framework separates recurring cash metrics from expansion capex and models CoreWeave contract-level lifetime returns rather than applying peer EBITDA multiples. He expects eventual competition and power supply to reduce scarcity returns but avoids a precise collapse date. Later Equinix growth was stronger than the reported early 2026 plan, while Lumen's legacy decline remained visible.
review.assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Nick Del Deo. Most forecasts and valuation estimates belong to Del Deo; Eisman asks clarifying questions and restates accounting concepts.
framework_points: Map property ownership, equipment ownership and customer obligations separately.
Distinguish network effects from temporary physical scarcity.
Value GPU projects over equipment life, including capex, financing, renewals and residual value.
Lifetime NPV per invested dollar is not an annual return on capital.
Check final user latency separately from latency inside a training cluster.
Deduplicate utility requests and distinguish planned, contracted and energized power.
tools_and_charts: Capital cost per MW excluding IT equipment
REIT taxable income versus AFFO and cash flow
ROIC minus cost of capital and reinvestment volume
CoreWeave GPU contract DCF and $65 valuation
Lumen conduit value and Cogent wavelength revenue
transcript_cautions: Opening montage repeats body claims.
All 1771 caption lines were read.
Nick Del Deo and company names are frequently garbled.
Recording appears materially earlier than October 22 publication: Core Scientific bid is described as recent and CoreWeave quoted near $90. Exact date not established.
The $40b equipment figure against a $14b-$15b contract may be a caption or spoken-number error and is not silently corrected.
The 2025 $5.3b revenue and 2026 AFFO path are forecasts at the time, not realized premises.

review.title: The K-Shaped Reality: AI Booms While Housing & Tesla Struggle | The Weekly Wrap
review.summary: The October 24 wrap compares strong AI-linked equipment demand with weak housing and managed care. It discusses Tesla expectations, credit-score competition and efficient scale businesses, while directing viewers to bank earnings supplements.
review.assessment: The operating contrast is useful and supported by several issuer releases. GE Vernova orders are confused with backlog, and the FHFA policy is incorrectly described as requiring both FICO and VantageScore. Strong company results are kept separate from investment-return forecasts.
framework_points: Follow order conversion in long-cycle equipment.
Compare organic and acquired growth.
Separate valuation expectations from current operations.
Learn the actual regulatory rule before extrapolating competition.
transcript_cautions: Netflix EPS comparison is internally garbled in the captions; no exact-number error is assigned from that passage.
Tesla robot and robotaxi targets are reported Musk statements, not Eisman forecasts.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

review.summary: Andrew Ross Sorkin discusses the human incentives and policy failures surrounding 1929. Eisman emphasizes leverage, shared institutional exposures, short-selling survival and the danger of assuming officials already understand a crisis. This is mainly historical explanation, not a prediction of another crash. Original Fed records contradict the guest's assertion that policymakers could not contemplate rate increases in 1929, and preexisting bank capital rules qualify the repeated no-rules narrative.
review.assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Andrew Ross Sorkin. Historical explanations by the guest are kept separate from Eisman's crisis framework and retrospective process revision.
framework_points: Map leverage, shared assets and funding links before calling a downturn systemic.
Separate correct bearish direction from the ability to survive a short.
Do not assume policymakers possess all available information or can act promptly.
Distinguish the crash, the ensuing depression, the start of recovery and full employment.
Use historical analogies as risk prompts rather than deterministic forecasts.
Check original policy actions before inferring motives from a narrative.
tools_and_charts: Bank capital and reserve rules before modern ratios
Layered leverage in old trusts and modern vehicles
transcript_cautions: Opening montage repeats the interview.
All 1500 caption lines were read.
Biographical trivia and speculative mental-health characterization are omitted as immaterial to the investment audit.
Eisman's initial unemployment number is immediately corrected and accepted, so it is not a separate forecast error.
Book anecdotes remain unresolved where the underlying archives were not inspected.
Sorkin explicitly says he is not forecasting another 1929.

The more ambitious Meta-versus-cloud-provider return comparison is not established by market capitalization or cash-balance changes alone. His company differentiation is stronger than blanket claims that rate cuts or AI announcements always help stocks.
framework_points: Distinguish current cloud revenue from uncertain future monetization.
Check funding capacity as capex rises.
Differentiate a strong sector from a weak business model within it.
Separate guidance, earnings quality and price reaction.
tools_and_charts: Operating cash flow and free cash flow
transcript_cautions: Microsoft equity-method passage is incomplete in captions; no missing wording is reconstructed.
Company guidance is retained as management guidance, not awarded as Eisman forecasting success.

review.summary: Eisman discloses a speculative Glass House holding and explores a low-cost greenhouse producer's profitability, raid recovery and federal-reform upside with management. Production recovery and eventual NYSE listing have evidence, but cash generation remained weak and broad interstate/export upside was conditional. The important legal distinction is that Schedule III alone does not open unrestricted trade; Farrar explicitly qualifies Kazan's earlier overstatement.
review.assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews CEO Kyle Kazan, president Graham Farrar and CFO Mark Vendetti. Management claims are separated from host adoption and questions.
framework_points: Separate a low-cost operating thesis from a policy catalyst.
Normalize seasonal costs, nonrecurring profits and disputed taxes before calculating ROE.
Model volume, realized price and margin separately; more production need not mean more cash.
Distinguish state permission, federal registration, exchange eligibility and export permits.
Treat management superlatives and illustrative capacity revenue as assumptions rather than verified forecasts.
Check whether commodity competition erodes the price spread underlying expansion plans.
tools_and_charts: Cost per pound and seasonal production
Gross, operating and adjusted EBITDA margins
transcript_cautions: All 1242 caption lines were read.
Opening montage repeats interview claims.
Names and financial abbreviations have ASR errors;18ish% matches operating margin, not adjusted EBITDA margin.
Management allegations and compliance representations are not adjudicated facts.
2026 retail deconsolidation changes comparable revenue.
The April 2026 medical-only rule must not be described as blanket legalization.

review.title: Cracks Beneath the AI Boom: Is the U.S. Economy Heading For a Downturn? | The Weekly Wrap
review.summary: The November 7 wrap connects narrow equity leadership with a divided economy, reviews AI expectations and warns that expensive stocks need more than merely good results. It also revisits FICO competition and explains banking money creation.
review.assessment: His warnings about valuation expectations and product differentiation are useful. The no-sales-force Palantir description is false, and the money-creation lesson conflates deposits, capital and reserves. Equity-index concentration is observable but does not itself prove that the rest of the economy has stopped growing.
framework_points: Look beneath capitalization-weighted headline indexes.
Distinguish operating growth from what the valuation requires.
Avoid shorting solely because a successful company is expensive.
Prefer differentiated products over easily substituted hardware.
transcript_cautions: The stated Monday November 4 date is inconsistent with the 2025 calendar; no investment verdict rests on the weekday slip.
The no-sales-force claim is adopted from Dan Ives and explicitly attributed as such.
review.speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.claim: Cooling labor conditions and concentrated affluent spending make the economy vulnerable to a stock-market correction.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track real spending by income, employment and wealth sensitivity.
claims.reason: The vulnerability is conditional, and the reported top-decile spending share needs a defined dataset. Distributional stress does not itself establish an imminent recession.
claims.next_check: Track real spending by income, employment and wealth sensitivity.

claims.claim: Equal-weight indexes reveal market participation concealed by megacap weights.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use matching total-return series and rebalance conventions.
claims.reason: A capitalization-weighted average and an equally weighted average answer different questions. The return gap measures dispersion in contributions, subject to rebalancing.
claims.next_check: Use matching total-return series and rebalance conventions.

assumptions: Use the same constituent universe and time interval.
proof.proof: Cap weighting gives more influence to larger initial weights; equal weighting assigns equal initial weights. Their return difference reveals the effect of weighting, not directly the GDP contribution of each firm.
proof.derivation: Cap weighting gives more influence to larger initial weights; equal weighting assigns equal initial weights. Their return difference reveals the effect of weighting, not directly the GDP contribution of each firm.

claims.claim: A return gap worse than the recent roughly ten-percentage-point norm should trigger greater concern.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Test the threshold against future drawdown and earnings breadth.
claims.reason: The rule has no precise forward-risk measure or horizon and is not calibrated as a forecasting model.
claims.next_check: Test the threshold against future drawdown and earnings breadth.

claims.claim: Top-heavy index performance proves a K-shaped real economy.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare market concentration with independent employment, spending and GDP data.
claims.reason: It demonstrates stock-market concentration; firms listed in the index and their weights do not map directly to household incomes or domestic value added.
claims.next_check: Compare market concentration with independent employment, spending and GDP data.

assumptions: Market capitalization reflects expected global equity cash flows, not current domestic output.
proof.proof: An index can become concentrated through valuation changes without a corresponding shift in current household income or GDP. Therefore market concentration alone cannot prove a particular real-economy distribution.
proof.derivation: An index can become concentrated through valuation changes without a corresponding shift in current household income or GDP. Therefore market concentration alone cannot prove a particular real-economy distribution.

claims.claim: A Mamdani administration may hurt New York property and encourage business relocation.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track enacted policies, rents, employment and net relocations.
claims.reason: He flags potential consequences rather than a dated net-outflow prediction. A flat election-day stock response is not proof that all costs were already priced.
claims.next_check: Track enacted policies, rents, employment and net relocations.

claims.claim: AI earnings growth remains strong but analysts have caught up, making beats less powerful for stocks.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare forecast errors, estimate revisions and valuation across releases.
claims.reason: This requires a consistent surprise and revision dataset rather than selected reports.
claims.next_check: Compare forecast errors, estimate revisions and valuation across releases.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Read sales practices and selling expense disclosures.
claims.reason: The pre-episode filing explicitly describes its direct sales force and sales organization. The adopted guest explanation overstates organic distribution.

evidence.title: Palantir Q2 2025 filing
evidence.finding: The filing explicitly describes a direct sales force and efforts to build sales operations. Word of mouth and bootcamps do not mean the company has no sales force.

claims.next_check: Read sales practices and selling expense disclosures.

claims.reason: The explanation needs product-specific comparisons; data platforms and databases are not interchangeable in every workflow. Reported customer anecdotes do not establish universal superiority.
claims.next_check: Compare use cases, deployment cost, measurable outcomes and competing products.
